items.title: Shared-Prefix KV Reuse Across Standard LoRA Adapters: Quality and Serving Tradeoffs
items.summary: This research investigates shared-prefix KV reuse across standard LoRA adapters to optimize small-model deployments by preventing redundant context prefilling. It analyzes the quality and serving tradeoffs of this optimization technique.

items.title: MOCC-R1: Reinforcing Reasoning-Response Consistency for Multimodal Counselor Response Generation
items.summary: This research introduces MOCC-R1, a method for reinforcing reasoning-response consistency in multimodal counselor response generation. It aims to improve the generation of appropriate counselor responses from multimodal dialogue histories by addressing dataset limitations.

items.title: Extracting ontology-compliant knowledge from scientific text describing irradiated materials using large language models
items.summary: This research applies large language models to extract ontology-compliant knowledge from scientific texts describing irradiated materials. It aims to make essential data from scientific literature more accessible for predictive models and simulations in materials science.

items.title: Causal neural set filtering for online multi-target tracking
items.summary: This research proposes Causal Neural Set Filtering (CNSF) for online multi-target tracking, addressing redundant computation in transformer-based trackers. The method aims to jointly learn data association and state estimation more efficiently.

items.title: Managing Action Preconditions in Neuro-Symbolic RL: Three Placement Strategies for Embodied Agents
items.summary: This research explores three placement strategies for managing action preconditions within Neuro-Symbolic Reinforcement Learning for embodied agents. It aims to enable agents to leverage prior behavioral knowledge for more efficient learning in new tasks.

items.title: OmniHarness: Harnessing Generalizable Visual Generation via Symbolic Policy Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces OmniHarness, a novel methodology for generalizable visual generation using unified multimodal large language models and multi-agent systems, addressing limitations in existing task-specific methods.

items.title: Driver Behavior Estimation at Signalized Intersections Using a Physics-Constrained Decision-Conditioned Autoregressive Transformer
items.summary: This paper presents a physics-constrained decision-conditioned autoregressive transformer to estimate and predict human driver decision-making and trajectory behavior at signalized intersections, aiming to mitigate traffic accidents.

items.title: HintMiner: Automatic Question Hints Mining From Q&A Web Posts with Language Model via Self-Supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes HintMiner, a novel tool using language models and self-supervised learning to automatically mine question hints from Q&A web posts, helping users find answers more effectively.

items.title: POSPAN: Position-Constrained Span Masking for Language Model Pre-training
items.summary: This paper introduces POSPAN, a new position-constrained span masking technique for language model pre-training, enhancing the benefits of span-level masked language modeling by addressing previous limitations in span length considerations.

items.title: A panoramic aerodynamic performance prediction method for turbomachinery cascades using transformer-enhanced neural operator
items.summary: This paper proposes a panoramic aerodynamic performance prediction method for turbomachinery cascades, utilizing a transformer-enhanced neural operator to enable flexible and rapid evaluation in design.

items.title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Semantics-Consistent Tabular Diffusion with Weak Semantic Priors
items.summary: This paper presents Semantics-Consistent Tabular Diffusion, a new method for generating synthetic tabular data that explicitly models weak semantic priors to ensure consistency, moving beyond mere distribution matching.

items.title: Schema-Adaptive Action-Conditioned JEPA for Cross-Machine CNC Transfer under Partial Sensor Overlap
items.summary: This paper studies Schema-Adaptive Action-Conditioned JEPA (SAAC-JEPA) for cross-machine CNC transfer, addressing challenges in deploying industrial world models across varying dynamics, sensing interfaces, and control units.

items.title: LLMs as Master Forgers: Generating Synthetic Time Series Data for Manufacturing
items.summary: This paper introduces a novel framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate synthetic time series data for manufacturing processes, addressing the scarcity of labeled data in real-world industrial settings.

items.title: Z-Loss Backward Geometry in Dense Output Heads and Sparse Routers
items.summary: This paper analyzes the application of Z-loss in language-model output heads and sparse mixture-of-experts routers, detailing how it constrains softmax log-normalizers to improve training stability and reduce roundoff exposure.

items.title: How I learned to stop worrying and love StopGrads: Stationarity, Convergence, and a case study on Flow Map Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces a stopgrad regression principle to theoretically ground the use of stopgrads in training machine learning models, investigating their impact on gradients, stationary points, and convergence guarantees.

items.title: Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder
items.summary: This paper proposes a new method, "Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder," to remove specific knowledge from trained Large Language Models (LLMs) without complete retraining, addressing limitations of existing weight-based approaches.

items.title: Efficient Reasoning Distillation: Small Video-Language Models via Synthetic CoT and Difficulty-Aware Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This paper presents an efficient method for 'Reasoning Distillation' to instill reasoning capabilities into compact video-language models (VLMs) for video question answering, using synthetic chain-of-thought and difficulty-aware fine-tuning.

items.title: Drift Field Net: Learning Ocean Lagrangian advection fields from in-situ and satellite observations
items.summary: This paper introduces Drift Field Net (DFN), a method for learning ocean Lagrangian advection fields from observational data to improve forecasts of particle drift, particularly relevant for plastic debris accumulation zones.

items.title: Robust Fault Detection in Mechanical Multimodal Time Series via Self-Supervised Cross-Modal Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper presents a method for robust fault detection in industrial systems by using self-supervised cross-modal reconstruction on mechanical multimodal time series data, aiming for early identification of abnormal behavior.

items.title: Generative models for simulation based filtering: Formulations and Empirical Comparisons
items.summary: This paper presents a unified formulation and numerical comparison of generative-model approaches for the nonlinear filtering problem. It analyzes how different approaches realize the analysis step by transporting the forecast distribution to the posterior.

items.title: Channel-Informed Neural Network for Physical Layer Key Generation
items.summary: This research proposes a channel-informed neural network for physical-layer key generation, enabling wireless devices to establish shared keys from reciprocal channel observations. This method is attractive for lightweight key establishment in resource-constrained edge networks.

items.title: Multi-Label Proportion Learning for Sea-Ice Type Prediction
items.summary: This paper addresses sea-ice type prediction, crucial for climate monitoring and maritime navigation, using multi-label proportion learning on manually produced ice charts from satellite imagery. It aims to improve prediction despite challenges from sparse and ambiguous label data.

items.title: Federated stochastic bilevel optimization with fully first-order gradients
items.summary: This paper investigates federated stochastic bilevel optimization, a method widely applied in machine learning, focusing on an approach that uses fully first-order gradients. It aims to address the computational burden of existing algorithms that often require second-order Hessian and Jacobian matrices.

items.title: Autonomous Droplet Navigation via Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This research explores autonomous droplet navigation in lab-on-a-chip platforms using model-based reinforcement learning. The goal is to achieve precise manipulation of liquid droplets through complex geometries, which is challenging due to their physical properties.

items.title: Certified Uncertainty Propagation in One-Shot Federated Bayesian Models via Posterior Event Transport
items.summary: This paper addresses the probabilistic certification of Bayesian neural networks by lower-bounding the posterior probability of a model satisfying a verifier-defined safety property. It applies posterior event transport to one-shot federated Bayesian learning, where aggregated parameters form the deployed model.

items.title: Bounded Adjustment with Reliability-Guided Embedding for Imbalanced Learning with Noisy Labels
items.summary: This paper introduces BARGE (Bounded Adjustment with Reliability-Guided Embeddings), a single-stage approach for imbalanced learning with noisy labels. It aims to prevent frequency correction from amplifying incorrectly labeled minority examples, a common failure mode in class-balanced learning.

items.title: Attention Mean Fields Predict Average Representation Dynamics and Reveal Context-Specific Computation
items.summary: This paper introduces a mean-field analysis of attention to predict average representation dynamics in language models. It aims to faithfully account for the evolving representation geometry of models as they run, revealing context-specific computation.

items.title: OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces OPD-Aha, a method for multimodal on-policy distillation that enhances multimodal reasoning by allowing a teacher model to evaluate student trajectories using rich visual evidence. The approach focuses on how student models misinterpret images early in their processing.

items.title: Decoder Design Matters for ECG Delineation
items.summary: This paper investigates the importance of decoder design for accurate Electrocardiogram (ECG) delineation, which identifies boundaries of P waves, QRS complexes, and T waves. It aims to improve AI models' ability to learn and interpret ECGs despite the scarcity of manual annotations.

items.title: FlowATC: Aircraft Trajectory Prediction via Flow Matching
items.summary: This paper presents FlowATC, a flow-matching architecture designed for robust aircraft trajectory prediction to support next-generation air traffic control. The model is trained exclusively on historical aircraft trajectories, without route labels or chart supervision.

items.title: What Does Layer-Importance Reveal About Transformers and State-Space Models?
items.summary: This paper investigates what layer-importance reveals about Transformers and state-space models (SSMs), the two dominant families of sequence models. It explores the transferability of analytical knowledge from Transformers to SSMs through the lens of layer importance, which underpins compression and selective fine-tuning.

items.title: On the Importance of Gating: Memorization vs. In-Context Learning in State Space Models
items.summary: This paper examines the importance of gating mechanisms in State Space Models (SSMs) to understand their role in memorization versus in-context learning. It compares SSMs to Transformers, noting SSMs' favorable computational characteristics despite lagging in performance on some tasks.

items.title: Divergence Timing and Cumulative Disagreement under KV-Cache Eviction
items.summary: This paper investigates the effects of KV-cache eviction on autoregressive generation by analyzing divergence timing and cumulative token mismatch. It derives an exact decomposition to understand how perturbations to conditional token distributions lead to cumulative disagreement.

items.title: Stable by Construction: Variational Latent Markov Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
items.summary: This paper develops a variational approach using latent Markov operators to improve neural PDE solvers for long-horizon prediction of time-dependent physical systems. It aims to address the accumulation of local errors and distribution shift inherent in autoregressive prediction.

items.title: GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?
items.summary: This paper introduces GrowMTP, exploring whether reinforcement learning (RL) can dynamically generate its own draft head for speculative decoding during post-training of large language models. It aims to address the bottleneck of autoregressive rollout generation, which dominates wall-clock time.

items.title: Right Direction, Wrong Step: Geometric Analysis of Finite-Step Failure in Looped Transformers
items.summary: This paper provides a geometric analysis of finite-step failure in Looped Transformers, which reuse shared layers for iterative latent reasoning. It investigates why additional iterations can reduce support for a reference answer, clarifying whether an update's direction is locally unhelpful or its displacement is too large.

items.title: Continuous-Time Machine Learning: A Unified Mathematical Perspective
items.summary: This paper introduces continuous-time machine learning as a unified mathematical framework for modeling temporal dynamics, particularly for arbitrarily sampled or long-range observations. It addresses the fragmentation of existing CT machine learning branches.

items.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Machine Learning Methods for Fault Detection and Line Identification in Electrical Power Grids
items.summary: This study evaluates machine learning methods for fault detection and line identification in electrical power grids, aiming to improve upon traditional relay protection systems for grids with renewable energy sources. It addresses the challenges of complex fault scenarios in modern power infrastructure.

items.title: The Functionalizer: Lossless Functional Decomposition for Subword Tokenization
items.summary: This paper introduces "The Functionalizer," a new lossless pre-tokenization method designed to overcome the limitations of standard subword tokenizers. It aims to prevent fragmented embedding spaces and lossy normalization of orthographic variations.

items.title: Single Document Extractive Summarization using Domination in Hypergraph
items.summary: This study proposes a novel method for single document extractive text summarization by leveraging the concept of domination in hypergraphs. It aims to extract relevant and important information from documents more effectively.

items.title: Comment on arXiv:2607.01233: Survivorship Bias in Published-Paper Baselines for Research-Idea Distributions
items.summary: This comment critiques a prior paper's methodology, highlighting a survivorship bias issue when using published papers as a human baseline to evaluate LLM-generated research ideas. It points out a potential flaw in the distributional evaluation.

items.title: Crash Narrative-Guided Countermeasure Recommendation Using Large Language Models: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Intersection Safety
items.summary: This paper introduces a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework that uses Large Language Models to recommend traffic safety countermeasures based on crash narratives. This approach aims to make identifying crash mechanisms and recommending solutions more scalable than traditional expert judgment.

items.title: NepKANUN: A RAG-Based Nepali Legal Assistant
items.summary: NepKANUN is introduced as an AI-powered, RAG-based legal assistant tailored for Nepali legal texts, built on a fine-tuned large language model. It aims to improve access to legal information in Nepal by providing precise and streamlined answers.

items.title: Nepali Legal Expertise through Generative and Extractive Pre-trained Transformers (NepLEGiT)
items.summary: NepLEGiT leverages generative and extractive pre-trained transformers to provide Nepali legal expertise, addressing challenges in accessing legal information and the shortage of legal experts in Nepal. It aims to overcome language barriers and information fragmentation.

items.title: State of Thought Enables Endogenous Reasoning
items.summary: This paper presents "State of Thought" (SoT), a new test-time compute approach for Large Language Models that enables endogenous reasoning. It aims to improve LLM capabilities by reducing reliance on external control or costly search space expansion.

items.title: Efficient Multimodal Generative Recommendation with Latent Narrative Reasoning
items.summary: This research paper introduces a new method for efficient multimodal generative recommendation that reformulates item prediction as semantic identifier generation, using latent narrative reasoning.

items.title: The Imitation Game: When LLMs Learn to Reason Like Programs via Code-Centric Reasoning Data Synthesis
items.summary: This paper proposes MIMIC, a framework that uses executable code to synthesize reasoning data, enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve deterministic, fine-grained reasoning capabilities.

items.title: RAG-CT: Mitigating Privacy Risks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Scanning Prompt Distribution
items.summary: This paper introduces RAG-CT, a method designed to mitigate privacy risks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems by scanning prompt distribution, aiming to prevent information leakage.

items.title: StalePO: Anchored Token-Level Preference Optimization using Legacy Post-Edits in Machine Translation
items.summary: This paper introduces StalePO, a method for anchored token-level preference optimization in machine translation, using legacy human post-edits to update newer models efficiently.

items.title: Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes using 'Register Tokens' to enable bounded-state reasoning in diffusion language models (dLLMs), allowing them to continue reasoning without keeping all generated text in context.

items.title: Negation Beyond the Verbal Channel: Temporal Multimodal Correlates in Dialogue
items.summary: This research investigates multimodal behavioral information, beyond linguistic realization, that correlates with negation cues in spoken dialogue.

items.title: ReMova: Fine-tuning LLMs for English to Belarusian translation
items.summary: This paper presents ReMova, a Belarusian-specific data-cleaning pipeline and fine-tuning methodology for English-Belarusian machine translation, addressing orthography and noise challenges.

items.title: Early-Bird Decoding: Accelerating Diffusion LLMs with Learnable Block Sizes and Parallel Sampling
items.summary: This paper introduces Early-Bird Decoding, a method to accelerate diffusion Large Language Models (LLMs) by using learnable block sizes and parallel sampling for more efficient inference.

items.title: Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data
items.summary: This paper proposes Style-Debiased DPO, a method for updating Large Language Model (LLM) knowledge by using factuality-aware synthetic preference data to improve recall and accuracy.

items.title: PunGraph: Retrieval-Enhanced Phonetic-Semantic Graph Reasoning for Pun Understanding
items.summary: This paper introduces PunGraph, a novel method utilizing retrieval-enhanced phonetic-semantic graph reasoning to improve Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to understand puns.

items.title: Quantifying Organizational Environmental Action from Web Data and Large Language Models
items.summary: This research presents a scalable computational framework using Large Language Models (LLMs) to quantify organizational environmental actions from public web data, addressing challenges in environmental data science.

items.title: Rewarding Reasoning, Not Answers: Fixing and Bounding Test-Time Reinforcement Learning on Medical QA
items.summary: This research investigates test-time reinforcement learning on medical multiple-choice QA, revealing that while effective in mathematics, it causes accuracy stagnation and reduced output diversity in a medical context. It analyzes the limitations and behavior of the method in this specific application.

items.title: DiaWhisper-DPO: Role-Attributed Transcription of Clinical Interviews via Failure-Mined Preference Optimization
items.summary: This paper introduces DiaWhisper-DPO, a method utilizing failure-mined preference optimization for role-attributed transcription of clinical interviews, specifically for automated depression screening. It focuses on accurately attributing utterances to clinicians or patients.

items.title: TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization
items.summary: This research introduces TIAO (Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization), a novel reinforcement learning method aimed at improving large language models' performance in text summarization. It focuses on condensing content while preserving consistency and coherence by being aware of token importance.

items.title: Smarter by the Moment: Environment-Driven Dynamic Policies for Continual LLM Improvement
items.summary: This research explores environment-driven dynamic policies for continual improvement of large language models, aiming to enable them to adapt to evolving tasks and environments. It addresses the limitations of existing memory-augmented approaches that retrieve individual examples.

items.title: A Data-free Universal Prior over Syntactic Structures
items.summary: This paper investigates the existence of a data-free universal prior over syntactic structures, exploring whether parts of language's probabilistic structure can arise independently of language-specific data. This has fundamental implications for theories of language and large language models.

items.title: Reduplicative constructions in Mandarin: Socio-emotional profiling through distributional semantics
items.summary: This study uses distributional semantics for socio-emotional profiling of reduplicative constructions in Mandarin Chinese, analyzing how the repetition of words or their constituents conveys varied meanings. It explores aspects like plurality, valence coloring, and pragmatic functions.

items.title: Cascade: Hierarchical Recoverability Control for Large Language Model Unlearning
items.summary: This research proposes 'Cascade,' a hierarchical recoverability control method for large language model unlearning, designed to remove sensitive or copyrighted knowledge. It aims to prevent residual knowledge from being recovered from intermediate representations, ensuring utility preservation.

items.title: Deconstructing Stereotypes: Scope-Conditioned Generation for Effective Multilingual Counterspeech
items.summary: This research introduces 'Scope-Conditioned Generation,' a method for generating more effective multilingual counterspeech to combat online hate speech. It aims to produce targeted and nuanced responses that deconstruct stereotypes, moving beyond generic replies.

items.title: Lit3R: Retrieve-Relate-Read for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Scientific Literature
items.summary: This paper describes Lit3R (Retrieve-Relate-Read), a system for evidence-grounded question answering over scientific literature, developed for the LitTraceQA shared task. Lit3R combines off-the-shelf retrieval, reranking, and large language models to identify evidence and generate answers.

items.title: Target-Language Generation in Multilingual Models: Activation Steering and Optimal Control
items.summary: This research develops an optimal control method, including activation steering, to enhance target-language text generation in multilingual models. It also proposes a framework for evaluating the quality of the generated text in specific target languages.

items.title: Nameless Tokenization: A Lossless Tokenizer-Level Defense Against Control-Token Forgery in Open-Weight LLMs
items.summary: This research proposes 'Nameless Tokenization,' a lossless tokenizer-level defense mechanism against control-token forgery in open-weight large language models. This defense aims to prevent manipulation of chat templates and reserved identifiers through prompt text.

items.title: Autoformalizing Argumentative Material Inferences
items.summary: This paper explores methods for 'autoformalizing argumentative material inferences' to make natural language arguments machine-checkable. It addresses the challenge of making implicit premises, warrants, and exceptions explicit for formal verification.

items.title: PaperDoctor: Evidence-Grounded and Actionable Feedback for Scientific Papers in Progress
items.summary: This paper introduces 'PaperDoctor,' a system designed to provide evidence-grounded and actionable feedback for scientific papers in progress. It aims to scale the process of identifying flaws and offering traceable suggestions, similar to human advisors.

items.title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs
items.summary: This paper studies counterfactual self-explanations in large language models to assess the faithfulness of their generated explanations to their actual behavior. It investigates how models minimally edit inputs to change their own predictions.

items.title: Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning with Entailment for Spatial Transcriptomics
items.summary: This paper explores Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning with Entailment as an AI method to improve the accessibility and scalability of Spatial Transcriptomics in biomedical research. It addresses challenges like high operational costs and experimental noise in gene expression mapping.

items.title: ProtoLIP: From Sentence-Level to Object-Level Evidence Disentanglement
items.summary: This research introduces ProtoLIP, a method for disentangling evidence in query-conditioned vision-language models to achieve more fine-grained, object-specific interpretations. It aims to improve how models reveal visual evidence in response to textual queries.

items.title: Sequence Recognition in Bharatnatyam dance
items.summary: This paper investigates sequence recognition in Bharatanatyam dance, focusing on identifying "Adavu" variations which comprise specific motions and postures. It applies AI techniques to analyze this traditional Indian classical dance form.

items.title: Reasoning with Image Generation
items.summary: This research explores integrating image generation with chain-of-thought reasoning to overcome limitations of text-only reasoning for tasks requiring visual manipulation. It aims to enable large language models to decompose problems using visual representations.

items.title: Decentralized Gossip Learning and Federated Averaging for Histopathology Image Classification
items.summary: This study compares decentralized gossip learning and server-based Federated Averaging for breast histopathology image classification, addressing privacy and governance constraints in distributed medical data analysis. It explores distributed learning techniques for healthcare applications.

items.title: Which Pretext Task Transfers? Self-Supervised Pretraining Objectives for Lung Ultrasound
items.summary: This study investigates which self-supervised pretraining objectives, such as contrastive learning or masked reconstruction, are most effective for lung ultrasound image analysis. It aims to reduce the reliance on labeled medical images by optimizing pretext tasks for self-supervised learning.

items.title: Vision And Text Transformer For Predicting Answerability On Visual Question Answering
items.summary: This research proposes a Vision and Text Transformer for predicting answerability in Visual Question Answering (VQA) tasks. It aims to provide more nuanced answerable scores between images and questions than traditional binary mapping approaches.

items.title: GraLoD: Graphics-Inspired Continuous Level-of-Detail Learning for Image Restoration
items.summary: This research introduces GraLoD (Graphics-Inspired Continuous Level-of-Detail Learning) as a novel method for image restoration. It addresses the varying spatial support required by different degradation types by learning representation scales dynamically, moving beyond fixed multi-scale hierarchies.

items.title: FLAT: Resampling Image and Text into 1D Flexible-Length Aligned Transmodal Tokens for Retrieval and Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces FLAT, a method for multimodal representation learning that resamples image and text into 1D flexible-length aligned transmodal tokens. It aims to improve generative performance by bridging the gap between traditional two-stage multimodal learning and generation.

items.title: G3AR: Graph-Guided Neural Visual Geometry for Scalable Multi-Sequence Aerial Registration
items.summary: This paper introduces G3AR, a graph-guided neural visual geometry framework designed for scalable multi-sequence aerial image registration, addressing challenges in processing thousands of images. It improves how irregular non-local overlap is handled in aerial collections.

items.title: JewelTry: Mask-Free Scale Aware Jewelry Virtual Try-On
items.summary: This paper presents JewelTry, a mask-free and scale-aware virtual try-on method specifically developed for jewelry, aiming to improve online shopping visualization despite challenges like small item size.

items.title: Can Knowledge Transfer Parameters Be Learned? LePoKet for Efficient Robotic Vision
items.summary: This paper proposes LePoKet, a method that learns knowledge transfer parameters from larger pretrained models to achieve efficient perception for robotic systems operating under computational constraints.

items.title: What Do Hallucinations Reveal About Multimodal Reasoning? Diagnosing Visual Grounding Failures via Contrastive Decoding Probes
items.summary: This research investigates what hallucinations reveal about multimodal reasoning in large vision-language models, using contrastive decoding probes to diagnose visual grounding failures.

items.title: SAVTrack: Selective Vote Aggregation for Reliability-Aware Point Cloud Tracking
items.summary: This paper proposes SAVTrack, a method for selective vote aggregation to improve reliability-aware 3D single object tracking in LiDAR point clouds, especially under sparse and incomplete observations.

items.title: Bridging the Perceptual Gap: Residual-Enhanced Downscaling and Manifold-Aware Perception Alignment Adaptation for NR-IQA
items.summary: This paper proposes a method to enhance No-Reference Image Quality Assessment by using residual-enhanced downscaling and manifold-aware perception alignment adaptation to bridge the perceptual gap in models like CLIP.

items.title: Lesion-centered 3D mapping of colonoscopy procedures: validation of a hierarchical ensemble pipeline on public benchmark videos
items.summary: This paper validates a hierarchical ensemble pipeline for lesion-centered 3D mapping of colonoscopy procedures, aiming to preserve spatial information from recorded videos that is typically discarded.

items.title: Efficient Quantization-Aware Distillation with Cross-Modal Alignment for Edge Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes an efficient quantization-aware distillation method with cross-modal alignment to enable the deployment of large vision-language models like CLIP on resource-constrained edge devices.

items.title: Efficient 3D Whole-Body PET Image Denoising via Conditional Rectified Flow With Optimized Sampling Strategy
items.summary: This paper proposes an efficient method for 3D whole-body PET image denoising using conditional rectified flow with an optimized sampling strategy to address noise in ultra-low-dose imaging.

items.title: MAETrack: Unleashing the Potential of Pretrained Geometric Priors for 3D Single Object Tracking
items.summary: This paper introduces MAETrack, a method that leverages pretrained geometric priors from self-supervised 3D encoders to improve 3D single object tracking, addressing limitations in direct fine-tuning.

items.title: PriorPose: Reference-Guided Joint Deformation and Alignment for Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
items.summary: This paper proposes PriorPose, a method for category-level object pose estimation that employs reference-guided joint deformation and alignment to accurately recover similarity transforms for unseen instances.

items.title: De-GAN - Dynamic Parameter Tuned GAN for 3D Medical Image Segmentation: A Step Towards Generalisation
items.summary: This paper introduces DE-GAN, a dynamic parameter-tuned conditional GAN that combines input-adaptive dynamic convolutions for improved 3D medical image segmentation, specifically for brain tumors.

items.title: FSANet: Frequency-Spatial Aware Network for Image Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces FSANet, a Frequency-Spatial Aware Network designed for image segmentation that aims to improve performance under challenging conditions while being computationally efficient.

items.title: IMVS: Interactive Medical Volume Segmentation with Test-Time Adaptation - A New Method for Annotating Radiology Datasets
items.summary: This paper introduces IMVS, an interactive method for medical volume segmentation that uses test-time adaptation to make the annotation of large radiology datasets more efficient.

items.title: Unifying Semantic Priors and High-Frequency Traces: Enhancing V-JEPA with Mixture-of-Experts for Robust Synthetic Image Forensics
items.summary: This paper enhances V-JEPA with a Mixture-of-Experts approach to develop robust synthetic image forensics, aiming to improve the detection of manipulated images and combat misinformation.

items.title: TEDi: Temporal Memory-Enhanced and Denoising Transformer for Surgical Instrument Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces TEDi, a Temporal Memory-Enhanced and Denoising Transformer designed for surgical instrument segmentation, which improves upon existing query-based methods by incorporating temporal information.

items.title: Hyper-RED: Scalable Event Pre-training via Semantic Hypergraph Distillation
items.summary: This paper proposes Hyper-RED, a method for scalable event representation pre-training that utilizes semantic hypergraph distillation to overcome the scarcity of large-scale annotated event data.

items.title: StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection
items.summary: This paper introduces StackTok, a method to accelerate VLM inference by using budget-adaptive visual token selection, reducing overhead without retraining.

items.title: FAHCD-Net: Frequency-Adaptive Heatmap-Conditional Diffusion Networks for Robust Facial Landmark Detection
items.summary: This paper proposes FAHCD-Net, a method using frequency-adaptive heatmap-conditional diffusion networks for robust facial landmark detection, particularly in challenging conditions.

items.title: RegRet: Enhancing Region-Level Retrieval in Large Multimodal Models
items.summary: This research introduces RegRet, a method to enhance region-level retrieval in Large Multimodal Models by aligning image regions with textual descriptions.

items.title: TecoPrompt: Temporal-Conservative Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes TecoPrompt, a temporal-conservative prompt-learning framework that addresses label noise during few-shot supervision for Vision-Language Models like CLIP.

items.title: Measuring Annotation Efficiency for Handwritten Devanagari Recognition: Sample-Complexity Curves for Four Pretraining Regimes
items.summary: This research measures annotation efficiency for handwritten Devanagari recognition using sample-complexity curves across four pretraining regimes.

items.title: tcnerv:dual-domain temporal context modeling for implicit neural video compression
items.summary: This paper introduces tcnerv, a dual-domain temporal context modeling method for implicit neural video compression, aiming to minimize reconstruction distortion.

items.title: SPEAR NeXT Causal Latent Forecasting Across Multiple Horizons for Spectral Temporal Earth Representation Learning
items.summary: SPEAR NeXT is introduced as a pixel-wise multimodal spectral temporal foundation model for Earth representation learning, focusing on causal latent forecasting.

items.title: NeuroTS-Net: Multi-Class Semantic Segmentation of Pediatric Brain Tumors in Multi-Modal MRI
items.summary: This paper presents NeuroTS-Net, a method for multi-class semantic segmentation of pediatric brain tumors using multi-modal MRI, to support diagnosis and treatment planning.

items.title: Accelerated Decoding of Centroid Positional Encoding for Instance Segmentation
items.summary: This research focuses on accelerating the decoding of centroid positional encoding for instance segmentation, aiming to reduce the significant execution cost of this stage.

items.title: Multi-modal Knowledge Preserving Adapter for Embedding Backward Compatibility
items.summary: This paper introduces a multi-modal knowledge preserving adapter to ensure embedding backward compatibility, addressing the issue of costly database re-indexing when upgrading embedding models.

items.title: PiPS: Post-Hoc Prototypical Explanations for Interpretable Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces PiPS, a method for post-hoc prototypical explanations to achieve interpretable semantic segmentation, enhancing trust in deep neural networks.

items.title: NeuroSymbEAD: A Large Scale Neuro-Symbolic Caption Dataset for Omni-Directional Embodied Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper introduces NeuroSymbEAD, a large-scale neuro-symbolic caption dataset featuring an ego-centric knowledge graph, designed for omni-directional embodied autonomous driving.

items.title: Geometry vs Structure: Graph-Based Diagnostics for LiDAR Point-Cloud Simulation Fidelity
items.summary: This research proposes graph-based diagnostics to quantify the fidelity of LiDAR point-cloud simulations, which are used to validate autonomous-driving and advanced driver-assistance system (ADAS) sensor pipelines.

items.title: Differentiable Mesh State Estimation via Factor Graph Inference for Deformable Object Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper proposes a novel factor graph-based framework for differentiable mesh state estimation, enabling probabilistic reconstruction of deformable objects, a fundamental challenge in robotics and simulation.

items.title: World Models for Embodied Intelligence: From Plausible to Controllable to Actionable
items.summary: This paper discusses the role of world models in embodied intelligence, highlighting their function in connecting perception and decision-making by anticipating consequences and adapting to improve behavioral capabilities.

items.title: The Robot Data Factory

items.summary: An initiative called 'The Indian Indigenous AI Model Map' is being discussed, likely pertaining to an overview or categorization of AI models specific to India.

items.summary: This article examines how artificial intelligence is transforming the MBA classroom, highlighting a real-world application of AI in the education and business sector.

items.title: AI is exciting audit firms — maybe too much
items.summary: This article notes the rapid adoption of AI by audit firms like KPMG and EY for their operations, while emphasizing the continued necessity for human involvement in the process.

items.title: TimeThink: Eliciting Compositional Reasoning in Timeseries Large Language Models
items.summary: TimeThink is a proposed method aimed at improving compositional reasoning in Timeseries Multimodal Large Language Models (TS-MLLMs), addressing their current limitations in capturing dynamic temporal patterns.

items.title: Governing at Machine Speed: An Adaptive Intelligence Architecture for Real-Time AI Policy Enforcement
items.summary: This paper proposes an adaptive intelligence architecture for real-time AI policy enforcement within organizations, addressing the gap between AI adoption and governance infrastructure. It aims to help organizations produce auditable evidence for their governance policies.

items.title: Fraglingo: Molecular Design via Attachment-Aware Autoregressive Fragment Generation
items.summary: Fraglingo is an AI method for molecular design that uses attachment-aware autoregressive fragment generation. It aims to mirror how chemists make edits to optimize molecular properties by extending scaffolds or replacing substituents.

items.title: Toward a Decision-Assurance Layer for AI-Assisted Flight Planning in Air Traffic Management
items.summary: This research explores the development of a decision-assurance layer for AI-assisted flight planning in Air Traffic Management (ATM). It aims to mitigate risks associated with non-deterministic outputs of generative AI tools to ensure safety and operational reliability.

items.title: Planning or Learning: Reliability and Cost in Multi-Asset Maintenance
items.summary: This research compares planning-based and reinforcement learning (RL) approaches for optimizing reliability and operational cost in multi-asset industrial maintenance systems. It addresses the challenge of balancing these factors in complex, interacting systems.

items.title: Causal multi-modal AI for personalized chemosensitivity prediction
items.summary: This paper presents a causal multi-modal AI model designed to predict personalized chemosensitivity for breast cancer patients. It aims to improve treatment predictions beyond current guidelines, which may lead to overprescription of chemotherapy.

items.title: FLoKD: Adaptive Knowledge Distillation for Federated Low-Rank LLM over Wireless Networks
items.summary: FLoKD introduces an adaptive knowledge distillation method for federated low-rank LLMs operating over wireless networks. It addresses privacy concerns in conventional centralized LLM fine-tuning by enabling collaborative learning.

items.title: Solar Intelligence
items.summary: Solar Intelligence is a hybrid retrieval-augmented system designed to provide comprehensive decision support for solar energy. It aims to overcome limitations of fragmented data dashboards and general-purpose language models in the solar domain.

items.title: Safety as a Constraint: Fine-Tuning a LLM Recommender to Explain Itself
items.summary: This research explores fine-tuning an LLM recommender system with safety as a constraint to enable it to explain its recommendations. The goal is to enhance user service and increase the likelihood of user engagement by providing personalized evidence.

items.title: FedV-KGQA in Practice: Design Lessons and an Interactive Prototype
items.summary: This poster presents design lessons and an interactive prototype for FedV-KGQA (Federated Knowledge Graph Question Answering) in practice. It addresses challenges arising from distributed facts across organizations with disjoint relation types.

items.title: Cost Characterization of Vertically Partitioned Federated Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: This paper characterizes the cost of querying vertically partitioned federated knowledge graphs, which are distributed across organizations owning disjoint subsets of relations.

items.title: Enhancing Event Candidate Acquisition for Event Linking
items.summary: This research focuses on improving the acquisition of candidate events for event linking, addressing challenges like ambiguous mentions and noisy arguments in text.

items.title: Drift-Constrained Optimization: Only Direction Matters in Fine-Tuning Instruct Models
items.summary: This paper proposes Drift-Constrained Optimization, a method for fine-tuning instruct models that specifies a behavioral drift budget to maintain existing capabilities while improving target performance.

items.title: Degraded but Not Entirely Ineffective: PE-Based Deformable Graph Neural Networks
items.summary: This research explores Position Embedding-Based Deformable Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to overcome limitations of traditional GNNs like over-smoothing and issues with long-range dependencies.

items.title: How Many Thoughts Can a Vector Hold? The Capacity of Reasoning by Superposition
items.summary: This paper investigates the capacity of fixed-dimensional latent states in large language models to hold intermediate computations for multi-step reasoning through superposition.

items.title: Surprising Effectiveness of Self-Demonstrations in Enhancing Schema-Ontology Mapping with LLMs
items.summary: This research demonstrates the effectiveness of self-demonstrations combined with LLMs for enhancing schema-ontology mapping, a challenge in integrating heterogeneous databases.

items.title: Bypass Observation: A Conceptual Design of a Non-Intrusive Layer-Wise Semantic Extraction Architecture
items.summary: This paper introduces Bypass Observation, a conceptual design for a non-intrusive architecture that extracts layer-wise semantic information from large language models via read-only observation heads.

items.title: ViperQ: Order Flow Pattern Recognition via Auction Market Theory for Reinforcement Learning Trading
items.summary: This paper presents ViperQ, a reinforcement learning trading system that utilizes order flow pattern recognition based on Auction Market Theory rather than just price-aggregate representations.

items.title: UniCAR-RL: Seeing Better before Thinking Deeper in Visual Mathematics
items.summary: This research introduces UniCAR-RL to improve Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in complex mathematical visual reasoning by enhancing fine-grained perception to prevent cascading reasoning failures.

items.title: Map Users and Mapmakers: The Scope of Cognitive Attribution from Acquired Representations
items.summary: This paper develops a framework for specifying how an acquired representation enlarges a system's cognitive repertoire and its limitations, introducing a five-part attribution table.

items.title: Synthetic Data in Marketing Research: How to Evaluate and When to Trust
items.summary: This paper discusses the evaluation and trustworthiness of synthetic data generated by large language models (LLMs) for marketing research, examining when such data can be effectively used.

items.title: Convergent Emergence of In-Context Learning Across Modalities
items.summary: This research investigates the convergent emergence of few-shot in-context learning (ICL), a model's ability to infer and apply patterns from prompt examples, across different modalities beyond large language models.

items.title: Schizophrenia Detection from EEG Signals: A Transformer Framework with Spectrogram Representation
items.summary: This paper proposes a Transformer framework utilizing spectrogram representation of EEG signals for automated schizophrenia detection, aiming to support clinical assessment.

items.title: VeriDx: Earning the Right to Diagnose with Disease-Centric Verification
items.summary: VeriDx is a system for disease-centric verification in clinical reasoning, designed to ensure correct diagnoses are reached through justified evidence checking, alternative exclusion, and contradiction resolution.

items.title: Semantic Knowledge Technologies: what the Semantic Web lost sight of, and what it never had
items.summary: This paper critically examines the Semantic Web's unfulfilled promise of machine-interpretable information and reasoning, contrasting its historical goals with current scientific knowledge systems.

items.title: A derivative-fidelity failure mode in physics-informed neural networks: strengthened benchmark evidence from function-value training
items.summary: This paper identifies a derivative-fidelity failure mode in physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), providing benchmark evidence that good function-value agreement does not guarantee accurate derivatives.

items.title: Early Prediction of Satellite Collision Probability Using a Hybrid TCN-Transformer Model for a CDM-Based Conjunction Analysis Framework
items.summary: This research proposes a hybrid TCN-Transformer model for the early prediction of satellite collision probability within a Conjunction Data Message (CDM)-based analysis framework, addressing increasing orbital debris in LEO.

items.title: Diagnosing Faults in Reinforcement Learning Simulators and World Models with Canonical Polynomial Invariants
items.summary: This paper investigates diagnosing faults in Reinforcement Learning simulators and world models by testing the premise that models respecting underlying physics predict better, using canonical polynomial invariants.

items.title: Algorithmic Information Dynamics of Learning: A Certified, Differentiable Complexity Controller for Grokking
items.summary: This paper introduces a certified, differentiable complexity controller for studying "grokking" in AI models, using Algorithmic Information Dynamics to analyze changes in algorithmic complexity during learning.

items.title: Discovering and Preserving Category Correlation Knowledge via Adaptive Reciprocal Knowledge Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces Adaptive Reciprocal Knowledge Distillation, a method designed to discover and preserve category correlation knowledge during knowledge transfer from large teacher models to smaller student models, especially with significant size gaps.

items.title: Criticality in Dissimilar Decomposition and Undersampling of Random Datasets with Anomalies
items.summary: This research investigates how the inclusion of AI-generated text/image data in training datasets affects batch decompositions and the performance of subsequent Large Language Models.

items.title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Still Need Feature Engineering?
items.summary: This paper explores whether traditional feature engineering remains necessary for tabular machine learning given the rise of tabular foundation models that are pretrained and applied via in-context learning.

items.title: Scalable partial information decomposition for symptom networks via supervised embeddings
items.summary: This research presents a scalable method for partial information decomposition using supervised embeddings to better understand complex relationships within symptom networks, particularly in mental health.

items.title: GradRepair-ODE: Certified Gradient Repair for Neural ODE Training
items.summary: This paper introduces GradRepair-ODE, a certified gradient repair method for Neural Ordinary Differential Equation training to address reliability issues caused by the coupling of numerical solvers and gradient computation.

items.title: Task-Aware Federated Fine-Tuning for MoE-based Large Language Models
items.summary: This research proposes a task-aware federated fine-tuning approach for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) based Large Language Models, optimizing their use in resource-constrained and distributed environments.

items.title: Specification Oracles
items.summary: This paper investigates the potential of using a language model as a compact, dynamic 'specification oracle' that can learn and provide facts about a target system, addressing the tradeoff between detail and conciseness in specifications.

items.title: ReCAST: Reward Credit Assignment across Timesteps for Online Diffusion Reinforcement
items.summary: This paper introduces ReCAST, a method for reward credit assignment across timesteps in online diffusion reinforcement, aiming to effectively train diffusion models with multiple rewards by distinguishing user preference from reward informativeness.

items.title: Certifiably Interpretable Training of ReLU-MLPs for Boolean Tasks with Guaranteed Truth-Table Generalization
items.summary: This research presents MACCHIATO, a specialized training algorithm for ReLU-MLPs that constructs certifiably interpretable models for boolean tasks with guaranteed truth-table generalization.

items.title: Learning to Solve Hard Problems in RL for LLMs by Never Giving Up
items.summary: This paper identifies the 'Matthew Effect' in RL for LLMs, showing that Reinforcement Learning disproportionately improves performance on easier problems while offering smaller gains for harder ones.

items.title: A Machine Learning API for Earth Observation Data Cubes Based on openEO
items.summary: This paper proposes a Machine Learning API based on openEO to bridge the gap between spatio-temporal Earth Observation data cubes and machine learning methods, facilitating reproducible data transformations.

items.title: On the Potential of Multi-Task Learning in Predictive Process Monitoring
items.summary: This research explores the benefits and potential of multi-task learning for improving prediction accuracy and proactive analysis in Predictive Process Monitoring of organizational processes.

items.title: One Spectrum, Two Resources: Data-Memory Scaling in Autoregressive Prediction
items.summary: This paper presents a theoretical finding on data-memory scaling in autoregressive prediction, showing that data and learned memory resources are governed by a single predictive-energy spectrum.

items.title: Pretraining for Sample-Efficient Neural Interfaces
items.summary: This research investigates the use of self-supervised pretraining to achieve sample-efficient neural decoders for Brain-Computer Interfaces, reducing the need for large labeled datasets per subject.

items.title: Adaptive Phase-Switching for Communication-Efficient Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This research introduces an adaptive phase-switching method to enhance communication efficiency during federated LoRA fine-tuning of large language models, addressing a major cost in distributed training.

items.title: Operational Range Bounding in Spectroscopy: A Safety Cage Framework for Machine Learning Models
items.summary: This paper proposes a 'Safety Cage Framework' for operational range bounding in spectroscopy, aiming to ensure the reliability of machine learning models in safety-critical applications like space missions.

items.title: GeoTTER: Leveraging Local Geometry of Optimal Transport for Zero-Shot Classification
items.summary: This paper introduces GeoTTER, a novel framework that redefines optimal transport by leveraging local geometry for improved zero-shot classification, addressing issues of miscalibration and adaptability.

items.title: Rolling Day-Wise Mortality Prediction in Critically Ill Patients With AKI on CRRT Utilizing Machine Pressure Waveforms
items.summary: This study focuses on improving mortality prediction for critically ill patients with AKI on CRRT by utilizing machine pressure waveforms in addition to standard clinical parameters.

items.title: Generative Interpretability via Scalable Neuro-Symbolic Models
items.summary: This paper advocates for 'Generative Interpretability' via scalable neuro-symbolic models as a more adequate approach for understanding AI systems, especially as LLMs move into agentic systems with real-world consequences.

items.title: Attention Is All You Need (to Avoid Spurious Oscillations)
items.summary: This research develops a conservative, fixed grid finite-volume scheme that incorporates a CFL-conditioned attention flux to move shocks across cells without spurious oscillations in numerical simulations.

items.title: Curvature-Independent Regret Bounds for Distributed Online Optimization on Hadamard Manifolds
items.summary: This research addresses decentralized online Riemannian optimization on Hadamard manifolds, focusing on curvature-independent regret bounds in optimization analysis.

items.title: Online Bayesian Node Classification on Inductive Graphs under Distribution Shift
items.summary: This work explores online Bayesian node classification on inductive graphs under distribution shift, aiming to achieve inductive generalization and calibrated uncertainty for evolving graph data.

items.title: Leakage-Safe and Scheduler-Aware Machine Learning for Grid Job Runtime Prediction
items.summary: This paper investigates leakage-safe and scheduler-aware machine learning models for predicting job runtime in grid and distributed computing environments, considering realistic deployment constraints.

items.title: PPDL: A Real-world Industrial User Retention Ratio Forecasting Framework Integrating Physical Priors with Deep Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes PPDL, a real-world industrial framework that integrates physical priors with deep learning to accurately forecast user retention ratios across multiple channels for optimizing budget allocation.

items.title: Graph Neural Networks for Influence Maximization in Social Networks: An Unsupervised Minimum Dominating Set Approach
items.summary: This research explores the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for influence maximization in social networks, applying an unsupervised Minimum Dominating Set approach for critical applications.

items.title: Lie to me: Detecting Managerial Evasiveness in Earnings Calls via Conversational Audio Encoders
items.summary: This study proposes a method to detect managerial evasiveness during earnings calls by leveraging conversational audio encoders to analyze vocal and lexical cues.

items.title: Machine Learning under Imperfect Data: Challenges and Methods
items.summary: This article provides an overview of the challenges and methods for machine learning under imperfect data conditions, where training and test data may be incomplete, unbalanced, or mislabeled.

items.title: Learning Through Energy Refinement and Manifold Projection: A Cooperative EBM-AE Framework
items.summary: This paper introduces a Cooperative EBM-AE Framework for generative modeling, leveraging Energy-Based Models (EBMs) to learn an energy landscape for realistic sample generation.

items.title: Token Merging for Multilingual Speech Recognition: A Systematic Study Across Model Scale and Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This study investigates token merging as a method to improve computational efficiency in multilingual speech recognition models like Whisper by dynamically combining redundant features.

items.title: Lexical Prompt Compression for Large Language Models: A Training-Free, Deterministic Pipeline with Empirical Pareto Analysis Across Eleven Task Categories
items.summary: This research presents a training-free, deterministic pipeline for lexical prompt compression in Large Language Models (LLMs) to reduce inference costs for increasingly complex prompts.

items.title: Clinical Reasoning Under a Partially Observed Objective in Cone Beam CT Report Generation
items.summary: This research explores clinical reasoning in maxillofacial report generation from cone beam CT scans, using a composite objective where LLM judgment and lexical overlap score the output.

items.title: RFCLLM: Evaluating LLMs' Reasoning Ability of Network Protocol State Machines
items.summary: This work evaluates Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to reason about network protocol state machines, focusing on their capacity to map textual specifications into formal representations.

items.title: Causal Analysis and Mitigation of Spurious Onsets in Full-Duplex Speech LLMs
items.summary: This paper presents a causal analysis of spurious speech onsets in full-duplex speech-to-speech LLMs like Moshi and PersonaPlex, proposing methods for their mitigation.

items.title: Hindsight Bias in Clinical Temporal Reasoning: How Future Data Exposure Affects Large Language Model Judgment
items.summary: This research investigates hindsight bias in clinical temporal reasoning by Large Language Models, examining how exposure to future data in retrospective records affects their judgment.

items.title: A Hybrid Hierarchical 1D-CNN-BiLSTM Framework for Extractive Summarization of Biomedical and Clinical Text
items.summary: This paper proposes a Hybrid Hierarchical 1D-CNN-BiLSTM framework for extractive summarization of biomedical and clinical text, aiming to avoid hallucinations common in abstractive methods.

items.title: Harmfulness Propagation Dynamics: Layer-wise Trajectories of Adversarial Intent in Large Language Models
items.summary: This research identifies 'Harmfulness Propagation Dynamics' (HPD), a phenomenon where the projection of harmful intent monotonically rises across transformer layers in Large Language Models.

items.title: Domain-Specific Jargon in Large Language Models: A Comparative Analysis between General-Purpose and Specialist Models
items.summary: This paper conducts a comparative analysis of how general-purpose and specialist Large Language Models (LLMs) handle domain-specific jargon and encode parametric knowledge.

items.title: Toward Complete Hospital Discharge Summarization with Abstract Meaning Representation
items.summary: This research explores generating complete hospital discharge summaries using Large Language Models (LLMs) augmented with Abstract Meaning Representation to mitigate hallucination.

items.title: The University of Melbourne WMT 2026 CreoleMT Submission: A Domain-Balanced Approach to Low-Resource Pacific Creole Machine Translation
items.summary: This paper details the University of Melbourne's WMT 2026 CreoleMT submission, focusing on a domain-balanced approach for low-resource machine translation of Pacific creoles like Tok Pisin and Bislama.

items.title: LayerRoute: Adaptive Layer-Skipping with LoRA-Preserved Quality for Efficient LLM Inference
items.summary: This paper introduces LayerRoute, a parameter-efficient method that combines adaptive transformer layer-skipping with joint LoRA fine-tuning for more efficient Large Language Model (LLM) inference.

items.title: Not all Negation Cues are Equal: Affixal Negations Yield Better Negation Understanding
items.summary: This research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) understand negation, finding that affixal negations lead to better comprehension compared to single-word negation cues.

items.title: When Edit Localization Amplifies Relative Selection Bias: Gradient Geometry, Target Mismatch, and Importance Weighting
items.summary: This paper analyzes how localized human corrections can amplify relative selection bias in models by examining gradient geometry, target mismatch, and importance weighting.

items.title: Scaling Hindi Quantum Natural Language Processing through Automatic Pregroup Supertagging
items.summary: This paper presents a method for scaling Hindi Quantum Natural Language Processing by using automatic pregroup supertagging to translate grammatical structures into quantum circuits for grammar-sensitive compositional models.

items.title: Inside VLM Chart Reading: Tracing Value Reading from Vertical Bar Charts Across Space and Depth
items.summary: This research paper investigates how vision-language models process information to answer questions about vertical bar charts, using activation patching to trace value reading in models like Qwen2.5VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL3.5-8B.

items.title: SyRHM: Symbolic-Language-Enhanced Reasoning with Associative Retrieval for Zero-shot Harmful Meme Detection
items.summary: This paper introduces SyRHM, a framework that combines symbolic-language-enhanced reasoning with associative retrieval to improve zero-shot detection of harmful memes by addressing implicit intent.

items.title: CRITICS - Critical Science Without Borders: Language Models to Promote Critical Thinking in Science Education
items.summary: The CRITICS project leverages advanced Large Language Model-based Machine Translation to improve science accessibility and literacy, aiming to promote critical thinking in science education.

items.title: Unlocking the Unsolvable: Teacher-Guided Curriculum for Data-Efficient RLVR
items.summary: This paper proposes a teacher-guided curriculum for data-efficient Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to enhance the mathematical reasoning capabilities of large language models, particularly for problems beyond their current capacity.

items.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Setting Inference Depth from the Questions a Deployment Actually Asks
items.summary: This paper explores how to optimize the inference depth of transformer language models by tailoring computation to the specific questions a deployment asks, rather than applying a uniform, potentially excessive, computation per token.

items.title: Learning to Refer from Estimated Listener Gaze
items.summary: This paper presents a method to finetune vision-language models for generating more pragmatically optimal referring expressions by using estimated listener gaze as a learning signal indicating incremental comprehension.

items.title: Corpus Characterization and Inverse Constitutional Fine-Tuning for Style-Aware Radiology Reports
items.summary: This research details a method called Inverse Constitutional Fine-Tuning, alongside corpus characterization, to improve the stylistic alignment of automatically generated radiology reports with authentic radiologist writing.

items.title: Editorial routing shapes how computational results are qualified in AI-assisted scientific writing
items.summary: This study investigates how editorial routing, a human intervention in AI-assisted scientific writing, influences how computational results are qualified and presented in draft manuscripts by large language models.

items.title: Theseus in the Graph: Towards Traceable Multi-Hop Graph Navigation
items.summary: This paper introduces a method called 'Theseus in the Graph' to enable traceable multi-hop graph navigation in Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems, allowing for explicit modeling and validation of intermediate reasoning steps.

items.title: Neyshekar: An Open Persian Read-Speech Corpus for Automatic Speech Recognition
items.summary: This paper presents Neyshekar, an open Persian read-speech corpus specifically designed for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), encompassing both formal and informal language, named entities, and longer utterances.

items.title: Personalized and Explainable Blood Pressure Estimation from PPG via Hybrid CNN--Morphological Features
items.summary: This research proposes a personalized and explainable method for continuous cuffless blood pressure estimation using photoplethysmography (PPG) via hybrid CNN and morphological features for improved healthcare monitoring.

items.title: Part Grounding, Not Action Knowledge: Locating the Bottleneck in VLM Affordance Prediction
items.summary: This research analyzes the bottleneck in vision-language model (VLM) affordance prediction for low-level manipulation, concluding that the limitation lies more in part grounding than in action knowledge.

items.title: Synthetic Leprosy Image Generation Using Mask-Conditioned Latent Diffusion and Transfer Learning from Large Chronic Wound Datasets
items.summary: This paper demonstrates the generation of synthetic leprosy images using mask-conditioned latent diffusion models and transfer learning from chronic wound datasets, aiming to address data scarcity for medical machine learning in neglected tropical diseases.

items.title: Don't Just Look, Intervene: Perturbation Based Region Labeling for VQA Images
items.summary: This paper introduces a perturbation-based region labeling method for Vision Question Answering (VQA) images, aiming to generate model-causal visual evidence to improve the grounding and interpretability of Vision Language Models (VLMs).

items.title: What Does the Encoder Actually Decide? A Controlled Comparison of Vision Backbones on Joint Tree Segmentation and Stereo Depth
items.summary: This research paper compares the performance of various vision backbones for joint tree segmentation and stereo depth estimation, particularly relevant for robotic tree pruning. It investigates the impact of encoder choice on performance under controlled conditions.

items.title: Occlusal Geometry in Closed Form for Orthodontic Report Generation
items.summary: This research proposes a system for orthodontic report generation from intraoral data by exploiting directly measurable occlusal quantities from registered scan pairs. This approach aims to provide more direct measurements rather than inferring quantities.

items.title: Pixel-wise Planarity for High-Precision Monocular Plane Segmentation
items.summary: This research proposes a pixel-wise planarity prediction framework for robust and high-precision monocular plane segmentation from single RGB images. It aims to overcome issues of imprecise region grouping and geometric inconsistencies.

items.title: Evaluation of MLLM-Agnostic Plug-and-Play Keyframe Selection Methods for Long Video Understanding
items.summary: This research evaluates various MLLM-agnostic plug-and-play keyframe selection methods designed to improve multimodal large language models' understanding of long videos. It addresses the computational limitations of MLLMs when processing extensive visual data.

items.title: (How) Do MLLMs Report Bistable Images Like Humans?
items.summary: This research investigates whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) report bistable images similarly to humans and explores the internal computations involved. It compares MLLM interpretation patterns with human perception of ambiguous stimuli.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of Multimodal Facial State Analysis: Tasks, Methods, and Resources
items.summary: This paper provides a comprehensive review of multimodal facial state analysis, covering various tasks, methods, and resources in the field. It discusses the challenges of traditional unimodal approaches and the benefits of multimodal analysis.

items.title: Sampling headroom is not selection gain: a compute-value audit of test-time scaling for video world models
items.summary: This research conducts a compute-value audit of test-time scaling (TTS) for video world models, analyzing whether additional computational effort consistently leads to better generation quality. It distinguishes between sampling headroom and selection gain in model performance.

items.title: Interpretable Temporal Video Reasoning with EventGraph and EventField
items.summary: This research presents a structured temporal video reasoning pipeline built around a discrete EventGraph, a continuous EventField, and a human-readable EventGlyph view. It achieves high accuracy on a calibrated EPIC-KITCHENS dataset.

items.title: Multi-View Structure-from-Motion Enables Oriented Projective Shape Analysis in Three Dimensions
items.summary: This research presents a geometric framework using multi-view Structure-from-Motion to enable oriented projective shape analysis in three dimensions. It provides a method for studying landmark configurations in digital images from pinhole cameras.

items.title: Variational Template Matching with Statistical Fusion for Anomaly Detection in Patterned Structures
items.summary: Proposes a novel variational template matching method with statistical fusion for anomaly detection in structured images. This approach offers robustness to geometric variations, addressing challenges in small-data settings.

items.title: Adaptive Conformal Redistribution for Inter-class Transitional Uncertainty in Medical Image Classification
items.summary: Presents a method called Adaptive Conformal Redistribution to address inter-class transitional uncertainty in medical image classification. It aims to make uncertainty-aware prediction sets more actionable in clinical settings.

items.title: RIGOR: Rig-Informed Geometry for Omnidirectional Reconstruction
items.summary: Presents RIGOR, a method for rig-informed geometry that improves omnidirectional 3D reconstruction from image streams. It aims to maintain consistency over long trajectories in challenging environments.
