items.title: When Connected Does Not Mean Similar: Charting the Homophily Boundary of SNAP-KG for Streaming Entity Integration
items.summary: SNAP-KG is a framework for assigning newly arriving entities to semantic communities in a growing knowledge graph (KG) using only their raw features, with no graph access and no retraining at inference time. It was evaluated on five multi-view benchmarks and a 2.4M-node OGB-WikiKG2 KG. In each of these datasets, at least one graph view is homophilous, meaning that connected nodes usually belong to the same class, and SNAP-KG performs well on all of them. This paper asks what happens outside that setting. We extend the evaluation to three heterophilous graphs (Texas, Wisconsin, Chameleon) and measure the edge homophily of every view. When no homophilous view is available, clustering quality drops sharply for both SNAP-KG and the transductive baselines used in its original evaluation. What decides this is the homophily of the relation, not the number of relations. Multi-view fusion still helps, but only when at least one homophilous relation provides a reliable foundation. The homophily assumption is therefore shared by the whole method family, not specific to SNAP-KG. We argue that heterophilous multi-view clustering is a separate research problem, outside the scope of this work. As future work, we outline how a heterophily-aware teacher could be distilled into SNAP-KG's projector to serve both homophilous and heterophilous KGs.

items.title: LatentVerse: A Framework for Understanding Shared and Modality-Specific Information in Multimodal Latent Representations
items.summary: Latent embeddings have become a central data abstraction in modern machine learning, especially in biomedicine, where foundation models are increasingly used to encode multimodal data like clinical text, medical images, omics, and physiological signals. However, the utility and value of these representations depends on understanding their quality, structure, and the information they encode. Existing analysis workflows for evaluating representations remain fragmented across custom scripts, isolated metrics, and most importantly lack multimodal analysis, limiting accessibility and reproducibility. We present LatentVerse, a representation analysis resource that combines a web-based visual analytics platform for accessible, report-driven exploration with a command-line interface for scalable technical workflows. LatentVerse unifies diagnostics for various representation quality metrics and extends to multimodal settings by decomposing embeddings into shared and modality-specific components. We evaluate LatentVerse through controlled unimodal and multimodal simulations, discovery-oriented analyses on real biomedical embeddings, and a user study across diverse use cases. By supporting thorough and interpretable evaluation of latent spaces, LatentVerse makes foundation model representations more understandable in biomedical and data science applications.

items.title: Certified AI Triage of ICU Alarms
items.summary: In the VTaC benchmark 71% of ventricular-tachycardia alarms are false, but silencing a real one can delay recognition of a dangerous arrhythmia. We reframe alarm reduction as three-way triage (retain, suppress, or defer) and bound the decision this analysis treats as harmful: among suppressed alarms, the fraction that were genuine stays below a user-set budget with 95% confidence, under i.i.d. event sampling. Alarms sharing a waveform record are dependent, so the clustered analysis is a sensitivity check. On the official split a 5% budget certifies in all three seeds, suppressing 74.8% of false alarms while silencing 1.5% of genuine ones, at AUROC 0.953 and Challenge Score 83.33, numerically comparable to the strongest of the eleven published systems. Our central finding measures what multiplicity costs: the correction charges for every candidate, so a finer grid can certify strictly less. Under held-out calibration the 885-cell grid we declared certifies 1 of 15 fold-runs, while choosing the grid on a separate selection partition certifies 8. We project the calibration volume each budget needs, making an uncertifiable budget a design parameter. Finally, adding a learned reliability dimension to the policy grid did not sharpen the certified frontier.

items.title: MInTRL: Off-policy Intervention can boost On-policy RL
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards is typically performed on-policy, keeping training data close to the current policy but limiting learning to trajectories that the policy can discover itself. Off-policy methods such as supervised fine-tuning, on the other hand, can leverage external knowledge beyond the base model's capabilities, but may suffer from large distribution shift. The key challenge is thus to expand exploration without sacrificing learnability. In this work, we introduce Minimal Intervention Reinforcement Learning (MInTRL), which expands the exploration frontier through sparse, local interventions in otherwise on-policy rollouts. During generation, a judge-intervention policy periodically reviews the current policy's output, replaces erroneous suffixes with short corrections, and immediately returns control to the policy. During training, MInTRL adopts a sequence-level advantage-regression objective that eliminates the need for importance sampling. We show that sparse, local interventions can substantially improve coverage beyond finite-budget on-policy sampling while preserving the overall on-policy nature of the resulting trajectories. Across math and code benchmarks, MInTRL consistently outperforms standard on-policy and off-policy baselines. Ablations show that MInTRL remains effective with self-intervention and across different judge policies, while performance peaks at moderate intervention intensity, highlighting the importance of intervening minimally. These results establish minimal intervention as an effective paradigm for enhancing on-policy RL.

items.title: Granularity-Adaptive Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Reinforcement learning is now the standard way to train large language model agents on long-horizon tasks, where dozens of interdependent actions precede a single sparse reward. Critic-free, group-relative methods such as GRPO suit this regime, but they broadcast one trajectory-level scalar to every step and cannot say which decision drove the outcome. GiGPO recovers a step-level signal by grouping time steps that share an anchor state, yet it merges the step- and episode-level estimates under one fixed weight, spending the same resolution on a pivotal branching decision as on a routine, near-deterministic transition. We argue that the right resolution is state-dependent, and propose GACA, a critic-free estimator whose granularity follows an uncertainty-based criticality proxy. GACA scores every step by the negative log-likelihood its own rollout already records, then blends the two advantages with a per-step weight that grows with that score, so the gradient places more weight on the fine-grained signal at above-average NLL and on the episode-level signal below it. We derive an exact risk decomposition for the implemented mixture and show that sufficiently small modulation improves on fixed mixing under positive directional alignment. A separate conditional result bounds local action-value variation using expected NLL, while an error-projection analysis characterizes when mixing adds value beyond scalar uncertainty reweighting. On ALFWorld and WebShop, GACA improves task success over GRPO and GiGPO at both 1.5B and 7B scales.

items.title: Observation-Anchored Selective Assimilation for Longitudinal Tumor-State Proxy Forecasting in Post-Treatment Glioma
items.summary: Post-treatment MRI in patients with glioma provides serial observations for updating patient-specific tumor-state proxy estimates, but variable appearances and trajectories complicate forecasting. We formulate forecasting as an observation-aware digital-twin update in which an intermediate observation anchors the patient-specific state. Among 203 patients and 594 follow-up time points, a predefined no-new-treatment criterion retained 120 of 236 candidate triplets, split into 81/24/15 training/validation/test triplets at the patient level. Each time point was represented by a continuous voxel-wise tumor-state proxy map in [0,1] derived from MRI lesion labels. A SegMamba-based single-step forecaster predicted update proposals from multimodal source-state tensors. Observation-Anchored Selective Assimilation (OASA) retained the observed intermediate proxy as the state anchor and selectively applied updates through a validation-selected tiered case-level rule and voxel-wise soft gate. We compared initial-scan forecasting, rollout without assimilation, latest-observation persistence, direct prediction, OASA, OASA + calibration, and morphological dilation. Checkpoints, OASA rules, and calibration thresholds were selected using validation data only. Across three seeds on 15 held-out test triplets, OASA maintained Dice at $\tau$ = 0.2 comparable to persistence (0.6071 $\pm$ 0.0025 vs. 0.6070) while yielding numerically higher Dice at $\tau$ = 0.5 (0.4269 $\pm$ 0.0079 vs. 0.3981), with a small RMSE increase. Calibration increased Dice at $\tau$ = 0.2 to 0.6178 $\pm$ 0.0025, increased false-positive (FP) support (11,836$\rightarrow$18,663), and reduced false-negative (FN) support (22,107$\rightarrow$17,536). This reflects near-threshold support calibration rather than improved biological predictive capability. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/jsudg436/longitudinal-proxy-forecasting.

items.title: Beyond the Query: Do Retrieval Signals Improve Adaptive Multimodal RAG Routing?
items.summary: Adaptive RAG often uses retrieval-time signals to decide whether another retrieval, reranking, or multimodal step should run. We ask whether these signals add routing value once the query itself is already known. Across document, audio, and video RAG, we compare matched query-only and query+retrieval routers while holding the optional actions, router family, training procedure, and evaluation fixed. On the held-out final evaluation, adding the tested retrieval signals does not produce a reliable routing improvement over the query-only baseline. Some retrieval signals are associated with whether a later step will help, but that predictability does not consistently lead to bet- ter RUN/SKIP decisions. The main lesson is therefore methodological: retrieval-state features should not be credited with routing value unless they improve over a matched query-only control. Our results do not show that routing or retrieval state is generally useless; they show that the incremental value of retrieval signals must be demonstrated rather than assumed.

items.title: SAGE-Loop: Reliable Closed-Loop LLM-Driven AutoML with Trial-and-Correction and Adaptive Ensembling
items.summary: Automated machine learning (AutoML) is reshaping data-driven science and industrial practice, and as large language models are introduced into AutoML, pipeline reliability becomes as important as automation efficiency. However, existing AutoML still struggles to realize instant feedback and adaptive optimization during execution, so once a run drifts into a suboptimal or failed state, it lacks a process-level correction mechanism. The fundamental pathology lies in its one-way pipeline: intermediate failures are typically terminated or bypassed, while fixed paradigms often strengthen model generation but leave ensemble decisions static, weakening both execution reliability and the controlled use of structural diversity. This indicates that LLM-driven AutoML needs a closed-loop ability for trial-correction-improvement together with evidence-based use of model diversity. To this end, we propose SAGE-Loop, a reliable closed-loop, self-adaptive, LLM-driven AutoML framework that performs multi-round generation and validation for trial-and-repair, and adaptively selects ensemble strategies in both supervised and unsupervised tasks, thereby unifying how to generate with how to use models. Across 20 public datasets, SAGE-Loop consistently improves performance and stability on classification, regression, and clustering tasks. Additional results further show its ability to recover from execution failures and maintain robust pipeline behavior.

items.title: A Differentially Private Federated Proximal Optimization Framework for Customer Churn Prediction in Heterogeneous Federated Telecom Networks
items.summary: Customer churn is one of the major issues in the telecommunication industry. To predict customer churn, conventional centralized machine learning approaches have been widely used. This centralized approach requires customer data to be stored in a central repository, which raises privacy concerns and may violate data protection regulations. Federated learning addresses this problem by allowing multiple telecom operators to collaboratively train a global model without transferring their raw customer data. However, real-world customer data are often heterogeneous (non-IID), which may negatively affect the performance of standard federated learning. Trained models can also suffer from privacy attacks. To address those issues, we propose a Differentially Private (DP) based Federated Proximal optimization (FedProx) framework. All experiments were performed on two publicly available telecom churn datasets. We trained Federated Averaging (FedAvg), DP-FedAvg, FedProx, and the proposed DP-FedProx framework. For baseline comparison, we also used several centralized and local models. To evaluate the models, we employed seven widely used evaluation metrics. The experimental results show that the FedProx based models consistently outperform the FedAvg based models. Compared with the best centralized model, the proposed DP-FedProx framework achieves competitive prediction performance with only a small reduction in accuracy while providing privacy guarantees. To explain our model, we conducted SHAP analysis which shows that DP-FedProx method priorities revenue group features. These results indicate that the proposed DP-FedProx framework provides a practical balance between prediction performance and data privacy protection.

items.title: Temporal Recurrence Favors Fewer Layers
items.summary: In streaming tasks, recurrent models can carry latent computation across time, allowing each update to build on representations produced earlier. This raises a basic question: once temporal recurrence provides sequential computation across steps, how much depth is still needed within each step? Prior work has shown that recurrence can make shallow models competitive. We instead study this question as a compute-allocation problem, varying within-step depth, expert width, and the number of parallel experts per layer across several compute budgets. For each budget, we compare the best observed recurrent and non-recurrent allocations and the performance they achieve under approximately matched per-step computation. Across Sokoban and autoregressive FineWeb language modeling, we find that temporal recurrence shifts the best observed compute allocation toward substantially fewer layers, with comparable or better performance.

items.title: $\text{GSF-}\chi$: Global Stereochemical Fields for Chiral Graph Transformers
items.summary: Enantiomers share atoms, bonds, and pairwise distances yet can behave differently in chiral environments, so molecular encoders must respect atom relabelings and proper rotations without becoming blind to reflection. We introduce GSF-$\chi$, a graph transformer in which stereogenic units modulate all pairwise interactions rather than single out one atom as special. Each central or axial stereogenic unit creates a reflection-even phase field over all atoms, a handedness pseudoscalar $\chi$ sets the direction of a relative rotation on latent query--key blocks, giving a \textbf{Chiral-RoPE} that reflection inverts rather than leaves fixed. A $C_2$ projection separates mirror-even ECD peak counts and positions from mirror-odd peak signs. We prove the operator's even--odd decomposition and its annotation-inversion, permutation, and unit-order identities under explicit canonical-role conditions; property tests and a coordinate-reflection audit verify the laws end to end. GSF-$\chi$ leads every central-ECD output and improves axial Rotation and Symbol by $12.6\%$ and $7.9\%$ over the strongest baseline. Equal-budget controls attribute the Rotation advantage to global signed support rather than parameter or edge count; the $C_2$ projection yields exact enantiomer-pair consistency at a small raw-accuracy cost under complete supervision and becomes predictive when mirror supervision is scarce.

items.title: Quality-Constrained Routing over a Fixed Pool of Quantized Mixture-of-Experts Instances
items.summary: Quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) services can hold several pre-materialized instances of one base model, but quantization damage varies sharply across requests and bitwidths. Because instance materialization and replica counts consume memory and require slow reconfiguration, we treat them as upstream provisioning decisions and study routing within a fixed resident pool. Within this fixed-pool boundary, we route each request to maximize modeled throughput under a class-level expected quality-degradation budget and measured instance capacities. To predict this request-specific risk, we introduce FWP (Fragility-Weighted Perplexity), computed from prompt tokens on a reference-instance prefill and calibrated to candidate-instance degradation. Underlying FWP is an exact two-expert affinity--fragility decomposition and a conditional multi-layer top-$k$ expansion whose bias, interaction, route-change, separability, and higher-order terms remain explicit. Using these calibrated risks, a window-level linear program yields a signed reduced-reward score that is KKT-consistent with the LP optimum under optimal prices and primal-feasible tie allocation. On 88 extended Qwen prompts, complete W2, W3, and W4 instances quantizing all 6,144 expert blocks incur mean $\Delta$NLL of $0.9437$, $0.1832$, and $0.0513$. Under the same population and $\tau=0.1513$, FWP allocation reaches a $1.284\times$ offline model-based multiplier versus $1.253\times$ for request-agnostic mixing and $1.000\times$ for static W4, an incremental $2.5\%$ relative FWP gain.

items.title: SCOPE-OPSD: Fisher-Conditioned Privileged Subspaces for On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) scores student-generated prefixes with a solution-conditioned self-teacher, yet transfers supervision only through next-token probabilities. We ask whether the aligned final-layer discrepancy offers a useful second channel, and how to test that channel without confusing its geometry with auxiliary strength. SCOPE-OPSD projects the privileged teacher-student residual onto a frozen rank-64 factor estimated from residual covariance and language-model-head Fisher sensitivity. It reuses the forwards already required by OPSD and adds neither rollouts nor inference-time modules. A matched Random control preserves the structured factor's rank and nonzero spectrum and uses per-arm gradient-RMS calibration, isolating the effect of the data-dependent orientation. Across the complete 25/50/75/100-step trajectories for Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B, Structured is never below Pure OPSD, with strict gains in 11 of the 12 model-checkpoint combinations and an exact tie at 4B step 25. Structured also exceeds matched Random in 10 of the 12 combinations. At step 75 on Qwen3-1.7B, Structured exceeds matched Random by 1.39 Macro Avg@12 points in each of two independent training reruns. A cross-fitted diagnostic also shows 4.40 times greater held-out privileged-gap capture than the matched random orientation. The results support a compact, Fisher-conditioned privileged subspace for short-budget OPSD.

items.title: Clustering-Based Balanced Sampling and Allocation with Data Parallelism for High-Performance Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Instruction-tuning datasets for large language models (LLMs) are often large, redundant, and imbalanced, limiting efficient adaptation. Naive large-batch fine-tuning repeatedly includes overrepresented sample groups while weakly covering underrepresented but informative ones, especially under data parallelism (DP) across multiple GPUs. We propose CluSTER, a Cluster-aware balanced Sampling framework for Training Efficient data Reduction in DP instruction tuning. CluSTER curates a representative reduced dataset through gradient-space clustering and DP-aware balanced allocation, ensuring dual-level coverage across clusters and workers, while preserving the original data distribution by weighted update. As a result, CluSTER reduces redundant computation and improves training stability without compromising model quality. Across multiple instruction-tuning datasets, CluSTER reduces training time by up to 69.6% with almost no accuracy loss compared to prior sampling and data reduction methods. Code is available at https://github.com/kaist-dmlab/CluSTER.

items.title: Where Decoder Cosine Similarity Fails for SAE Feature Flow Discovery
items.summary: Foundation models are increasingly adapted through fine-tuning, model editing, and alignment procedures while retaining previously acquired capabilities. Understanding the internal computations that support these adaptations is therefore becoming increasingly important for continual model evolution. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) provide interpretable feature dictionaries for residual-stream activations and sublayer outputs, but it remains unclear how state features and update features interact to produce downstream residual features. In this work, we focus on MLP updates as a first test case. We construct a transition atlas of triples $s_k + u_j \rightarrow t_\ell$, where a residual-state feature and an MLP-update feature jointly predict a target residual feature, and validate candidate triples by ablating the decoded update feature. In a 20M-token Pythia-160M $L_7 \rightarrow L_8$ run, we find 38,125 strong ablation-effect transitions, but 88.0% have both state-target and update-target decoder cosine similarity below 0.7. As a preliminary cross-model check, a run of 20M-token Gemma-3-4B $L_{21} \rightarrow L_{22}$ causally validates only the top 30,000 ranked candidate triples by ablating the decoded update feature, and 53.6% of strong-effect triples have both state-target and update-target decoder cosine similarity below 0.7. The Gemma result is directionally consistent with Pythia, but weaker, since update-target cosine recovers many of the strongest Gemma effects and the run is not a full-atlas causal validation. Ultimately, our results suggest that feature flow atlases can serve as diagnostics of representation-update mechanisms and thereby inform tools for steering model updates. Future work will validate more complex patterns across layers, models, and SAE families.

items.title: New method enables AI for safety-critical situations
items.summary: The “HardFlow” algorithm could help generative AI models produce high-quality outputs that obey strict requirements when “pretty close” doesn’t cut it.

items.title: R2VC: Modular Fact-Checking with Retrieval, Verification, and Confidence Calibration
items.summary: Large language models are increasingly used for automated fact checking, but end-to-end prompting often entangles evidence retrieval, reasoning, and uncertainty estimation, making failures difficult to diagnose and confidence difficult to trust. We present R2VC, a modular retrieve, reason, verify, calibrate architecture for evidence-grounded fact checking with citations and abstention. R2VC combines hybrid sparse+dense retrieval over Wikipedia, a supervised fine-tuned and DPO-aligned generator that produces diverse structured verdict candidates, an external NLI cross-encoder for evidence-based candidate selection, and a lightweight sequence-level calibrator for confidence estimation and selective abstention. On FEVER, an 8B backbone with R2VC achieves 13.74% higher accuracy than baseline. Ablation studies show that verifier-based candidate selection and confidence calibration are the largest contributors to performance. Removing candidate selection drops FEVER accuracy to 76.24%, while removing calibration nearly doubles the Brier score to 0.161. A manual analysis of 250 errors further shows that retrieval failures, especially wrong-entity evidence, remain the dominant bottleneck. Together, these results show that modular fact-checking pipelines can substantially improve both predictive accuracy and confidence reliability in open-domain verification.

items.title: What Counts as a Mistake? Annotating Recitation Events in Quran Memorization Transcripts
items.summary: Checking Quran recitation from an ASR transcript requires distinguishing unresolved mistakes from repetitions, repairs, opening formulas and accepted spelling differences. We report a completed human annotation of 100 production recording cases: 348 scored units and 162 localized events across ten combined labels. An executable evaluator scores labels and word positions together. A plain diff reaches label-aware F1 0.525 and localization F1 0.826; adapted production cleaner/alignment components reach 0.518 and 0.786, with exact-span F1 0.505 for both. Correcting the adapter's word coordinates recovers all five annotated repetition events, showing why annotation interfaces must be checked before interpreting baseline failures. In a preliminary pilot, eight single 20-minute runs across three coding agents and eight models span label-aware F1 0.143 to 0.892: seven land far above every baseline, and one collapses below the naive diff from a missing normalization step. Across the six, 970 of 972 gold-event instances draw an overlapping prediction, so what remains is not detection but convention: span extent, and the labels whose boundary is stipulated by adjudication rather than visible in the text. Seven of 162 events defeat all six same-day runs, five of them one orthographic rule, and the strongest run still misses the same ones. No run annotated before building, so the pilot measures the algorithm half of the task only.

items.title: Extracting Dataset Mentions in Forced Displacement and FCV Documents: A Weakly Supervised Framework with LLM-Based Label Refinement
items.summary: Development and humanitarian organizations produce and support surveys, administrative registries, and other data resources to inform research, policy, and operations, yet systematically identifying where these datasets are referenced remains difficult. Such references are dispersed across research papers, project documents, humanitarian reports, and other unstructured text, limiting both the ability to trace data use and to identify potential gaps in data availability or dissemination. We present a weakly supervised framework for adapting dataset extraction to forced displacement and Fragile, Conflict, and Violence (FCV) documents without first constructing a large manually labeled training corpus. A lightweight model trained on general research literature generates candidate dataset mentions from unlabeled domain documents, which a frontier large language model (LLM) reviews in context, validating or rejecting candidates and correcting their extraction boundaries. The resulting annotations are supplemented with targeted synthetic and contrastive examples and used to fine-tune the lightweight model for large-scale extraction. We evaluate the resulting model on an independent gold-standard benchmark of 1,706 text passages spanning research, humanitarian, and operational documents. Across the full benchmark, the model achieves 74.1\% precision and 70.5\% recall at the mention level; among passages containing dataset references, precision reaches 89.5\%. At the passage level, the model achieves 88.2\% accuracy and 88.6\% specificity in distinguishing passages with dataset references from those without them. These results demonstrate a practical approach for constructing domain-specific supervision when labeled data are limited, and provide a technical foundation for larger-scale analysis of data use and potential gaps in the displacement data landscape.

items.title: The Cost of Compression: A Rate-Distortion Limit on Factual Hallucination
items.summary: Factual hallucination in closed-book question answering is often treated as a coverage problem: a model fails because the relevant fact is absent from its internal memory. This view misses a second source of error. Even when a fact has been observed, finite memory may force it to be stored only approximately. We study this effect through a simple coverage--compression model of factual recall. We consider an unstructured question-answering task with $N$ possible queries and $K$ possible answers. A learner observes $M$ training facts, compresses them into at most $B$ bits, and answers uniformly drawn test queries without retrieval. For a uniformly random ground-truth mapping, we prove $\mathcal{E} \geq \frac{M}{N}\delta^\star\!\left(\frac{B}{M}\right) + \left(1-\frac{M}{N}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{K}\right)$, where $\delta^\star(r)$ is the inverse rate-distortion function of a uniform $K$-ary source under zero-one loss. The two terms separate compression distortion on observed facts from missing coverage on unobserved facts. The bound gives a compact way to reason about selective memory, forced compression, structure, retrieval, abstention, and long-context organization. We study the predicted signatures with theory-implied simulations and controlled fact-injection probes in modern language models that vary fact load and effective trainable memory. The result is not a complete theory of hallucination, but an information-theoretic account of a separable failure mode: lossy recall of observed facts under finite memory.

items.title: Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering
items.summary: Presents a method to improve multi-hop question answering by repairing and reinforcing context-augmented knowledge graph reasoning for large language models.

items.title: Automated Detection and Structuring of Social Tipping Point Evidence in Climate related Documents: A Modular AI Framework
items.summary: Proposes a modular AI framework for the automated detection and structuring of social tipping point evidence within climate-related documents.

items.title: HypoKG: Evidence-Disciplined Biomedical Hypothesis Generation Beyond Endpoint Knowledge
items.summary: Introduces HypoKG, a system combining biological databases to enable evidence-disciplined biomedical hypothesis generation by large language models, addressing their reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Not All Speech Is Intent: Adaptive Self-Correcting Inference Layer for Post-ASR False Wake-Up
items.summary: Proposes an adaptive self-correcting inference layer to mitigate post-ASR false wake-up activations in conversational AI by refining intent decisions from speech input.

items.title: The House with a Million Windows: Interactive Fiction for Narrative Restorying
items.summary: Introduces "The House with a Million Windows," an LLM-based interactive fiction system designed to enhance narrative restorying and address challenges in AI-assisted writing.

items.title: Calibrated Ambiguity in Multimodal Language Models: Humans reach for cultural references, while models describe the picture
items.summary: This paper investigates how multimodal language models handle ambiguity compared to human communication, where ambiguity can be a generative resource rather than a bug.

items.title: SWARM: A Multilingual Human-Annotated Dataset for Russian Propaganda Detection in Search Engine Results
items.summary: This work introduces SWARM, a multilingual human-annotated dataset designed for detecting Russian propaganda in search engine results, expanding beyond typical social media analysis.

items.title: DuplexDrama: A Synthesized Dialogue Dataset with Scenarios, Full-Duplex Behaviors, Expressive Speech, and Sound Events
items.summary: This presents DuplexDrama, the first synthesized spoken dialogue dataset that includes complete persona settings, full-duplex behaviors, expressive speech, and sound events.

items.title: LLM-Enhanced Dual-Branch Learning for Large-Scale Multi-Label Text Classification
items.summary: This paper introduces an LLM-enhanced dual-branch learning approach for large-scale multi-label text classification, improving performance for documents with many candidate labels.

items.title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models
items.summary: This research reveals gaps in large language models' long-horizon procedural reasoning by testing them on tasks derived from application manuals, highlighting limitations of current benchmarks.

items.title: Expert-Space Exploration in MoE Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates Expert-Space Exploration in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Reinforcement Learning, focusing on improving expert selection beyond fixed components for post-training LLMs.

items.title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking
items.summary: SAS (Simple Attention Sparsification) is presented as a method for optimizing context ranking via end-to-end training to reduce the quadratic attention cost in pretrained Transformers.

items.title: Type Diversity Enables Transformers to Generalise Compositionally
items.summary: This research suggests that type diversity, rather than inherent limitations, enables Transformers to achieve compositional generalization, particularly in structural generalization.

items.title: PRISMA-LLM: An Empirical Reporting Framework for AI-Assisted Systematic Reviews
items.summary: PRISMA-LLM is introduced as an empirical reporting framework to standardize the auditing and reporting of workflows in AI-assisted systematic reviews, addressing inconsistent information.

items.title: Creating an Atomic User Model for Personality-Aware Large Language Model Interaction
items.summary: This research proposes creating an Atomic User Model to enable more sophisticated personality-aware interactions for large language model assistants, moving beyond simple preference summaries.

items.title: Beyond ID Embeddings: Process-Grounded Language Modeling for Cognitive Diagnosis
items.summary: This work introduces Process-Grounded Language Modeling as an alternative to ID-based embeddings for Cognitive Diagnosis Models, aiming for a more natural representation of learner cognition in personalized learning.

items.title: Diverse Minds, Divided Networks? Personality Composition, Polarization, and Collective Intelligence in LLM-Based Social Simulations
items.summary: This paper uses LLM-based social simulations to study online polarization and collective intelligence by analyzing the impact of personality composition.

items.title: Information Specialization and Constrained Synthesis in Multi-Agent LLM Forecasting: A Prospective Live-Study of the 2026 FIFA World Cup
items.summary: This study conducts a live evaluation of multi-agent LLM systems with specialized roles for forecasting, specifically for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, to assess the impact of information specialization.

items.title: Feature Recovery for Object Understanding After Irreversible Fire Damage
items.summary: This work focuses on a method for feature recovery to understand objects after irreversible fire damage, critical for hazard detection and content reconstruction.

items.title: Beyond Argmax: A Mechanistic Study of Semantic Retention in Frozen Foundation-Model Composition for Generalized Few-Shot 3D Segmentation
items.summary: This study mechanically investigates semantic retention when composing independently pretrained, frozen foundation models for generalized few-shot 3D segmentation tasks.

items.title: Single-Query Person-Centric Bimanual Hand-Object Interaction Detection
items.summary: This research presents a method for single-query person-centric bimanual hand-object interaction detection, aiming to identify interactions specific to an individual with both hands.

items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation
items.summary: USPLIT-VQA proposes a U-shaped split learning framework with contribution-aware weighted aggregation for Visual Question Answering, addressing privacy concerns in VQA systems.

items.title: When Ground-Truth Fidelity Matters: An Orchestrated UAS Framework for Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus Detection Using Vision Transformers and Machine Learning
items.summary: This research details an orchestrated UAS framework utilizing Vision Transformers and Machine Learning for the early detection of Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus in sweet corn production.

items.title: QuPAINT: Physics-Aware Multimodal Reasoning for Quantum Material Characterization
items.summary: QuPAINT is introduced as a physics-aware multimodal reasoning system for characterizing 2D quantum materials, assisting in localizing flakes and determining layer thickness from optical microscopy.

items.title: GSO-Net: Visual State Machines for Hazardous Freight Transfer Compliance at Petrochemical Logistics Nodes
items.summary: GSO-Net describes a visual state machine network for ensuring compliance during hazardous freight transfer operations at petrochemical logistics nodes, addressing safety-critical procedural adherence.

items.title: OphBiWSSD: Scaling Temporal Action Localization in Ophthalmic Surgeries with Bidirectional Weight-tied State Space Duality
items.summary: OphBiWSSD presents a novel approach for scaling temporal action localization in ophthalmic surgeries using bidirectional weight-tied state space duality to model high-frequency surgical maneuvers.

items.title: A Multimodal Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis using 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Clinical Data
items.summary: This research proposes a multimodal explainable deep learning framework for Alzheimer's Disease diagnosis, integrating 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging and clinical data.

items.title: An End-to-End Automated Pipeline for Controllable Crack Data Synthesis
items.summary: This paper presents an automated pipeline for synthesizing controllable crack data, crucial for deep learning-based crack inspection where real data is scarce. It addresses limitations of generic image-generation methods by offering better control over crack morphology.

items.title: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
items.summary: This research improves few-shot medical anomaly detection by combining Vision Foundation Models with CLIP, overcoming CLIP's lack of explicit spatial supervision for precise lesion localization.

items.title: Partition-Invariant Tuning for 3D Scene Understanding
items.summary: This paper introduces Partition-Invariant Tuning, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for pre-trained 3D point cloud foundation models. It addresses the substantial computational and storage costs associated with full fine-tuning for 3D scene understanding.

items.title: PhysioAI: Clinical Knowledge-Guided Semantic Supervision for Skeleton-Based Physiotherapy Action Recognition
items.summary: This research introduces PhysioAI, a method using clinical knowledge to guide semantic supervision for skeleton-based physiotherapy action recognition. It aims to support automated tracking of exercises in remote rehabilitation settings.

items.title: RoES: Rotational Equivariant Selective-frequency Fusion for Multimodal Images
items.summary: This paper proposes RoES, a method for rotational equivariant selective-frequency fusion of infrared-visible images. It aims to enhance robust multimodal perception by integrating complementary textural and thermal information.

items.title: LettuceVisSim: A Simulator That Generates Lettuce Image Time-series for Vision-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces LettuceVisSim, a simulator designed to generate labelled lettuce image time-series data for vision-based reinforcement learning. It addresses the scarcity of labelled crop images hindering AI development in controlled environment agriculture.

items.title: One Skill Does Not Fit All: Automatic Discovery and Taxonomy-Guided Routing of Frame-Selection Skills for Long-Video Question Answering
items.summary: This research proposes a method for automatically discovering and routing frame-selection strategies for Long-Video Question Answering. It addresses the limitation of applying a single strategy to varied question types in hour-scale videos.

items.title: RelateAnything: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Relation Prediction From Any Inputs
items.summary: This paper introduces a new approach to open-vocabulary relation prediction that moves beyond fixed predicate taxonomies. It allows for real-time relation prediction from diverse inputs, similar to open-vocabulary detection and promptable segmentation.

items.title: DRS-VPT: Directly Relocalizing in a Scan with Vision Point Transformers
items.summary: This paper presents DRS-VPT, a feed-forward transformer architecture for foundational image-to-scan registration. It predicts scan pose and point maps from query images and a 3D point cloud.

items.title: An Ultra-Widefield Swept-Source OCTA Dataset and a Polar-Gated Mamba Network for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces WOIVES, a new ultra-widefield swept-source OCTA dataset, and a Polar-Gated Mamba Network for retinal vessel segmentation. It aims to address the lack of public benchmarks and comprehensive evaluation for this task.

items.title: Detecting and Explaining Fake News Short Videos with Multimodal Content and Real-World Evidence
items.summary: This research focuses on developing methods for detecting and explaining fake news in short videos, using multimodal content and real-world evidence. It addresses the challenge of widespread misinformation on video platforms.

items.title: NOVA-GS: Noise-Aware View-Consistent Gaussian Splatting for Low-Light Novel View Synthesis
items.summary: This paper introduces NOVA-GS, a technique for 3D scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis under low-light conditions using Gaussian Splatting. It aims to mitigate issues caused by severe sensor noise and low signal-to-noise ratios.

items.title: Semantically Aligned Gradient-Driven Context-Preserving Image Editing
items.summary: This paper describes a method for instruction-guided image editing that ensures semantic verification and context preservation. It addresses issues of incomplete edits and spatial spillage in generative editors.

items.title: ExpertHTR: Unified Handwritten Text Recognition with Multi-Task Learning and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
items.summary: This paper proposes ExpertHTR, a unified vision-language framework for handwritten text recognition using multi-task learning and sparse Mixture-of-Experts. It tackles challenges posed by diverse and distributed datasets across languages and scripts.

items.title: Multimodal Floorplan Encoding: Learning Dense Modality-Invariant Representations
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for multimodal floorplan encoding to learn dense modality-invariant representations. It aims to enable learning systems to transfer across different floorplan formats for geometry-centric tasks.

items.title: GRACE: Adaptive Concept Erasure with Geometry-Guided Retention in Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper presents GRACE, a method for adaptive concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models while retaining desired geometry. It aims to remove sensitive concepts from models without excessive intervention.

items.summary: This research proposes certification methods to establish lower bounds for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning, enhancing robustness against adversarial state perturbations in safety-critical applications.

items.title: Story Imprinting: AI Assistants Absorb Traits from Human Characters They Resemble
items.summary: This study investigates how finetuning AI assistants, such as language models, on synthetic stories can influence their character and behavior in multi-turn conversations with users.

items.title: Measuring the Value of World-Model Updates: A Counterfactual Utility Protocol for Continual Adaptation
items.summary: This research proposes a counterfactual utility protocol to measure the true value of individual updates in continual world models, addressing how to determine if new data justifies changing the model.

items.title: When More Is Not Better: Component Anti-Synergy in a P300 Speller
items.summary: This study investigates component anti-synergy in P300 brain-computer interface (BCI) spellers, revealing that combining individually promising components does not always lead to improved performance for hands-free communication.

items.title: EGGROLL, Unrolled: Understanding and Improving Low-Rank Evolution Strategies at Scale
items.summary: This paper introduces EGGROLL, a method that makes evolution strategies practical for large language models by using low-rank Gaussian weight perturbations, and analyzes its computational and geometrical properties.

items.title: Topological Necessities: Mechanism-Invariant Strategic Subgoals for Cross-Embodiment Goal-Conditioned Control
items.summary: This research explores topological necessities for mechanism-invariant strategic subgoals in cross-embodiment goal-conditioned control, proposing a novel approach for long-horizon reinforcement learning.

items.title: EMMI: Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence for Communication-Efficient MLLM Inference via Fused Representation Compression
items.summary: This research introduces EMMI (Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence), a method enabling communication-efficient inference of multimodal large language models on resource-constrained edge platforms via fused representation compression.

items.title: The information geometry of large language models is shared, learned, and controllable
items.summary: This paper investigates the information geometry of large language models, using Fisher-Rao geometry to understand shared behaviors, learning processes, and how to controllably modify specific aspects without affecting others.

items.title: Beyond Solver Verdicts: Generative Reward Models for Autoformalization
items.summary: This research proposes generative reward models for autoformalization to overcome limitations of mathematical solvers in neurosymbolic systems, formalizing the concept of Verdict-Preserving-Unfaithfulness (VPU).

items.title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
items.summary: This research proposes a method using large language models with bidirectional multimodal fusion of sky images and time-series data for improved short-term solar forecasting of photovoltaic power and global horizontal irradiance.

items.title: LILA: Calibration-Free Structured Pruning of Large Language Models via Latent Spectral Geometry
items.summary: This paper introduces LILA (Latent-Informed Layer Analysis), a calibration-free method for structured pruning of large language models that scores neuron importance via latent spectral geometry to achieve hardware-efficient compression.

items.title: When does a spectral prior help graph learning? Connectivity-loss estimation under road-network disruptions
items.summary: This research investigates the utility of spectral priors in graph learning for estimating connectivity loss in road networks after multi-edge deletion, using graph neural networks to learn bounded corrections.

items.title: Legible Failures: Detecting and Repairing In-Context Binding Errors
items.summary: This research investigates legible failures in language models, focusing on detecting and repairing in-context binding errors by analyzing whether models fail to use information they hold versus lacking it entirely.

items.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Time-to-First-Spike Neural Networks
items.summary: This paper studies the expressivity of spiking neural networks, focusing on the time-to-first-spike model, using polyhedral geometry to understand their asynchronous and event-driven computational capabilities.

items.title: MUtE: A Dual Framework for Concept Erasure and Counterfactual Interventions
items.summary: This paper introduces MUtE, a dual framework for concept erasure and counterfactual interventions, designed to remove concept-specific information from representations to mitigate bias and improve model interpretability.

items.title: A Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model for Traffic Flow Prediction
items.summary: This research introduces a Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model designed for traffic flow prediction, aiming to improve future traffic dynamics inference and resource allocation efficiency in intelligent transportation systems.

items.title: Reification as a Transferable Vocabulary: Zero-Shot Link Prediction with Vanilla GNNs
items.summary: This research proposes a novel method for zero-shot link prediction in knowledge graphs by reifying the input graph, enhancing transferability for vanilla Graph Neural Networks.

items.title: Prevalence Determines Precision:Silent Contamination in Detector-Defined Datasets
items.summary: This paper analyzes how dataset precision in machine learning is influenced by true-positive prevalence in detector-defined datasets, highlighting silent contamination via Bayes' theorem.

items.title: Combining Synthetic and Real Data for Low-Resource Historical OCR: A Manchu Case Study
items.summary: This research explores combining synthetic and real data to improve Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for low-resource historical Manchu texts, an endangered language.

items.title: Generalized Score Matching for Parameter Estimation on Convex Domains
items.summary: This paper introduces generalized score matching as a tractable method for parameter estimation on convex domains, addressing the challenges of maximum likelihood estimation for unnormalized probabilistic models.

items.title: Particle GFlowNets: Rethinking Generative Marginalization Models
items.summary: This paper introduces Particle GFlowNets, efficient neural sampling models for any-order autoregressive modeling of discrete distributions, enabling fast posterior evaluation by learning marginal and conditional probabilities.

items.title: LoaDiff: Conditional Generation of Electricity Consumption Time Series for Energy Analytics
items.summary: This research presents LoaDiff, a conditional diffusion model for generating electricity consumption time series, aiding energy analytics by understanding evolving residential usage patterns.

items.title: RDDMPI: Residual Denoising Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Multivariate Time Series Imputation
items.summary: This research introduces RDDMPI, a Residual Denoising Diffusion Model for probabilistic multivariate time series imputation, crucial for recovering missing values in interdependent temporal data.

items.title: Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training
items.summary: This paper proposes Musec (MomentUm SpEctral Clipping), a technique to enhance the stability of Muon optimizers during large language model training, addressing instability caused by spectral flattening.

items.title: Data-Efficient Language Modeling: From Frontier Advancement to Principle-Guided Model Improvement
items.summary: This research details an autonomous program on data-efficient language modeling, focusing on how models learn from limited text to maintain capabilities and generalize effectively.

items.title: Think Before You Link: Rarity, Reasoning, and Retrieval in Multilingual Entity Linking
items.summary: This research investigates challenges in multilingual entity linking, especially for rare entities, proposing new knowledge-graph structural metrics beyond popularity to assess rarity and improve systems.

items.title: Multilingual in Name Only? Cultural and Linguistic Weaknesses of LLMs in Urdu
items.summary: This research analyzes the cultural and linguistic weaknesses of multilingual large language models when generating text in low-resource languages, using Urdu as a case study.

items.title: Analyzing Traditional and Neural Approaches to Multilingual Readability Assessment
items.summary: This paper analyzes and compares traditional and neural approaches, specifically transformer-based models, for multilingual readability assessment, considering their linguistic properties and performance.

items.title: Larger Context Window, Fewer Overcorrections: Optimizing Prompts and Batching for Minimal-Edit Grammatical Error Correction
items.summary: This research investigates optimizing LLM prompts and batching strategies, leveraging larger context windows to reduce overcorrections in minimal-edit Grammatical Error Correction.

items.title: Detectable Only Where It Is Confounded: What Verified Duplication Counts Say About Membership Evidence in Language Models
items.summary: This paper explores how prediction cost relates to membership evidence in language models, investigating whether unusually low prediction cost indicates a sentence was part of the training data.

items.title: Does Linguistic Structure Enrichment Enhance Coherence Assessment? Not With Current Architectures
items.summary: This research investigates whether enriching linguistic structure enhances coherence assessment in large language models, concluding that current architectures do not benefit from this approach.

items.title: LLM-Anchored Paralinguistic Enrichment for Alzheimer's Disease Detection
items.summary: This research explores using LLM-anchored paralinguistic enrichment to enhance speech-based automatic detection of Alzheimer's disease by analyzing atypical pauses and word elongations.

items.title: Structurally Speaking: Motif-Oriented Graph Captioning through Bidirectional Graph-Text Translation
items.summary: This research proposes a motif-oriented graph captioning method that translates graph structures into textual descriptions, abstracting connectivity into recognizable patterns like hubs, paths, and cycles.

items.title: Using Semantic Uncertainty to Estimate Transition Relevance in Turn-taking
items.summary: This research investigates using semantic uncertainty to estimate transition relevance in turn-taking within Spoken Dialogue Systems, aiming to improve the timing of responses by anticipating appropriate speaking opportunities.

items.title: Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Modalities via Semantic-aware Completeness based Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper presents a robust multimodal sentiment analysis method that handles incomplete or noisy modalities by employing semantic-aware completeness-based reconstruction to prevent performance degradation.

items.title: Distribution-aware Language Neuron Identification in Multilingual Large Language Models
items.summary: This research focuses on identifying distribution-aware language neurons in multilingual large language models, studying how specific feed-forward neurons are sensitive to particular languages within the model's architecture.

items.title: K/V-Cache Interventions Dissociate Representation Alignment from Persona Expression in Decoder-Only Language Models
items.summary: This research explores K/V-cache interventions to dissociate representation alignment from persona expression in decoder-only language models, demonstrating a structured surface for persona control in models like Llama-3.1-8B.

items.title: Rebalancing Token Importance in Language Models with TF-IDF Weighted Cross-Entropy Loss
items.summary: This paper proposes a TF-IDF weighted cross-entropy loss to rebalance token importance during language model training, aiming to prevent frequent, low-information tokens from dominating learning and reduce memorization.

items.title: Rubric-Aligned Disentangled Evaluation of Human Simultaneous Interpreting
items.summary: This research focuses on developing an automatic, rubric-aligned, disentangled evaluation metric for human simultaneous interpreting, designed to assess meaning transfer, delivery quality, and temporal synchrony.

items.title: Automated Identification of Competing Narratives in Political Discourse on Social Media
items.summary: This research focuses on the automated identification and analysis of competing narratives within political discourse on social media platforms, aiming to understand how public opinion is influenced by evolving narratives.

items.title: OmniHallu: Unified Hallucination Detection for Cross-Modal Comprehension and Generation in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: OmniHallu introduces a unified hallucination detection method for Multimodal Large Language Models, addressing the issue of generated outputs contradicting or misrepresenting input semantics across various tasks and modalities.

items.title: The Illusion of Balanced Multimodal Sentiment Analysis: Beyond the Limits of Optimization-Based Methods
items.summary: This paper critically analyzes the limitations of optimization-based methods in addressing modality imbalance in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis, proposing a unified evaluation framework to re-examine balancing strategies.

items.title: Automatic Lyric Transcription for Greek Songs: Scaling and Task Composition Effects in Whisper Adaptation
items.summary: This research investigates automatic lyric transcription for Greek songs, a challenging task due to melodic variability and low-resource language status, by adapting and evaluating the Whisper model.

items.title: MultiHuSE: A Multimodal Dataset for Humour Styles and Emotions
items.summary: MultiHuSE introduces a new multimodal dataset for studying humor styles and emotions, providing resources for computational recognition of verbal humor which requires understanding language, delivery, emotions, and cultural context.

items.title: On the Impact of Anonymization on the Performance of Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper studies the impact of anonymizing input data on the performance of large language models, a critical practice for privacy in sensitive domains. It presents a systematic empirical analysis of this effect.

items.title: SEAR: Segment-Evidence-Aware Routing for Weak-to-Strong Multilingual Speech MCQ
items.summary: This paper describes the SEAR system for the Multilingual Conversational Speech Language Model Challenge, adapting Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct for weak-to-strong multilingual speech Multiple Choice Question Answering. It details a segment-evidence-aware data and post-training pipeline.

items.title: Cross-Lingual Clinical Annotation Projection as Constrained Text Generation: A Six-Language Study
items.summary: This study investigates whether cross-lingual clinical annotation projection can be framed as a text-preserving, document-level generative task for multilingual clinical corpus construction. It characterizes the robustness and computational aspects across six languages.

items.title: Structural priors for data-efficient language learning
items.summary: This research investigates structural priors for data-efficient language learning, aiming to reduce reliance on large data and computational resources. It explores training models on non-language data to induce useful priors for natural language processing.

items.title: Complex-Text Robustness Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis for Low-Resource Multilingual Text-to-Speech
items.summary: This paper addresses the insufficient diagnosis of robustness in low-resource multilingual text-to-speech (TTS) systems when handling complex text inputs. It proposes methods for evaluation and failure diagnosis beyond standard test sentences.

items.title: A Training-Free, Alignment-Free Approach to Corporate Intelligence: Application to SEC Filings
items.summary: This paper presents a training-free and alignment-free approach to corporate intelligence, specifically applied to SEC filings. It aims to overcome limitations of high-dimensional dense text embeddings and large language models in financial analysis.

items.title: Structured Transforms for Low-Overhead Quantization of Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes an improved algorithm for Kashin-decomposition-based weight quantization of large language models, featuring stronger convergence properties and structured, efficient orthogonal transforms. This method aims to reduce the overhead of language model deployment.

items.title: Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws
items.summary: This paper introduces Negative Self-Distillation, a new paradigm for large language model self-improvement. It enables models to learn reasoning by actively avoiding identified flaws, contrasting with traditional positive self-distillation.

items.title: The Eloquence submission for Task 2 of the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge
items.summary: This paper details the Eloquence team's approach for Task 2 of the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge, focusing on multilingual Multiple-Choice Question Answering. It describes methods including fine-tuning Voxtral-Mini-3B with LoRA.

items.title: LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces LOCUS, a method for task-aware low-rank post-training that aims to achieve token-efficient language generation in large language models. It investigates how post-training updates can influence output sequence length and serving costs.

items.title: Component-Aware Differential Privacy for Federated Multilingual Speech-LLMs
items.summary: This paper proposes a component-aware differential privacy method for federated multilingual speech-LLMs, demonstrating that standard per-layer clipping is insufficient for these models. It aims to improve gradient fidelity in privacy-preserving training.

items.title: Recognizing Is Not Reversing: A Controlled Inversion Test of Fact-Preserving News Framing
items.summary: This paper investigates large language models' ability to analyze and rewrite news, specifically using a controlled inversion test to see if they can undo news framing while preserving factual content. It assesses their capabilities in complex text manipulation.

items.title: The widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research 2023 to 2026
items.summary: This paper highlights a widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research, observing that the rapid evolution of LLMs outpaces the slower development of clinical evidence for their assessment. It analyzes trends in medical AI research from 2023 to 2026.

items.title: Target leakage, not model class, explains reported accuracy in survey-based cardiovascular screening: a leakage-tiered audit of glass-box and tabular foundation models
items.summary: This paper conducts a leakage-tiered audit of cardiovascular screening models, concluding that target leakage, rather than the model class, explains the reported high accuracy in survey-based systems. It assesses glass-box and tabular foundation models.

items.title: IndicTriMix: Developing Language Identification Datasets and Models for Tri-Language Code-Mixing
items.summary: This paper introduces IndicTriMix, a project focused on developing new datasets and models for language identification in tri-language code-mixed text. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying languages in utterances that switch between multiple languages.

items.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper presents a multi-signal detection pipeline, combining fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classification, Monte Carlo Dropout, and temperature-scaled calibration, to detect hallucinations in Large Language Models.

items.title: Distance generalization in transformers: why bother with positional encoding?
items.summary: This research investigates distance generalization in transformers, specifically focusing on their performance when inter-token distances change between training and inference, and the role of positional encoding.

items.title: Meta-Learning for Data-Efficient Plant Growth Estimation via Vision Transformers and Fuzzy Clustering
items.summary: This paper proposes a meta-learning, few-shot regression framework combining Vision Transformer embeddings and fuzzy clustering for data-efficient plant growth estimation in greenhouse monitoring.

items.title: Two-Parameter Flow Map Learning for Continuous-Time Diffeomorphic Image Registration
items.summary: This research proposes a learning-based method using two-parameter flow maps to model autonomous ordinary differential equations for continuous-time diffeomorphic image registration in medical image analysis.

items.title: BodyCam-VQA: Enhanced Body-Worn Camera Video Captioning via Multimodal Reasoning and Probe Question Generation
items.summary: This research introduces BodyCam-VQA, an enhanced method for body-worn camera video captioning that uses multimodal reasoning and probe question generation to improve data processing for law enforcement.

items.title: New Evidence, Same Choice: Testing Physical Experiment Selection in Vision Language Models
items.summary: This study tests how Vision Language Models select information and make choices when presented with new evidence in physical experiment scenarios, assessing their reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Toward Interpretable Multimodal Fusion: Heat Conduction Modeling for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Joint Classification
items.summary: This research explores a heat conduction modeling approach for interpretable multimodal fusion of hyperspectral and LiDAR data, aiming to enhance land-cover classification by better handling long-range dependencies.

items.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Using VLMs to Reveal Systematic Classification Failures Under Real World Conditions
items.summary: This work explores using Vision Language Models to identify systematic classification failures in other models under real-world conditions, moving beyond traditional benchmarks for verification and validation.

items.title: A Multi-View and Confusion-Guided Ensemble Framework for Robust Synthetic Image Attribution
items.summary: This research proposes a multi-view and confusion-guided ensemble framework to robustly attribute the source model of generated synthetic images, addressing challenges from the increasing similarity among diffusion-based generators.

items.title: CEM-TUDASR: Computationally efficient multi-modality transformer based unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution approach
items.summary: This paper introduces CEM-TUDASR, a computationally efficient multi-modality transformer-based approach for unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution, to enhance low-resolution Wireless Capsule Endoscopy images.

items.title: SCINTILLA-SNN: A Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network for Perineural Invasion Prediction
items.summary: This paper introduces SCINTILLA-SNN, a Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network designed to predict perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma by identifying subtle cues in MRI images.

items.title: Uncertainty DMD: Restoring Diversity in Few-Step Autoregressive Video Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces Uncertainty DMD, a method designed to restore diversity in few-step autoregressive video distillation, which often suffers from diversity collapse and weakened motion dynamics.

items.title: Improving Faint Object Detection for Space Situational Awareness with Variational Autoencoders
items.summary: This paper presents a deep-learning pipeline using Variational Autoencoders to improve the detection of faint moving objects in optical space situational awareness imagery by automating star removal and background reconstruction.

items.title: SAMV-DUSt3R: Instance-Centric 3D Scene Decoupling from Sparse Multi-Views
items.summary: This paper proposes SAMV-DUSt3R, an end-to-end model that integrates SAM2 2D masks into MV-DUSt3R reconstruction using a Cross Flow Mask Block to improve instance-centric 3D scene decoupling from sparse multi-views.

items.title: Your Model Already Knows Don't Teach It, Learn to Ask It: Soft Prompting for Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This research explores soft prompting for few-shot adaptation of Vision-Language Models in out-of-domain object detection, comparing it against existing methods like discrete prompt optimization and LoRA fine-tuning.

items.title: Mi-Ripple: Restoring Images Degraded by Iterative AI Editing
items.summary: This paper introduces Mi-Ripple, a diagnosis-guided restoration workflow designed to suppress 'digital ripple' – grid-like and granular textures – that degrade images from iterative AI editing, while preserving image structure.

items.title: Predictive Multi-Landmark OCT Tracking for Increased Motion Robustness
items.summary: This research introduces a predictive multi-landmark OCT tracking method aimed at increasing motion robustness, addressing limitations in trackable velocity for markerless motion tracking with optical coherence tomography.

items.title: R4Tun: LLM-guided adaptive segmental tunnel lining segmentation in point clouds
items.summary: This paper introduces R4Tun, an LLM-guided adaptation framework that enhances automated, adaptive segmentation of segmental tunnel linings from 3D point clouds for infrastructure inspection.

items.title: Vision Transformer-Based Multi-Level Feature Fusion for Multi-Label Sewer Defect Classification
items.summary: This study develops a Vision Transformer-based multi-level feature fusion method to improve the automated multi-label classification of sewer defects for infrastructure condition assessment.

items.title: Brain-PACE: A Deep Siamese MRI Framework for Modelling Longitudinal Brain Acceleration
items.summary: This research introduces Brain-PACE, a Deep Siamese MRI Framework designed to model longitudinal brain acceleration, aiming to improve brain age estimation and understanding of brain health trajectories.

items.title: DINO-Med: A Unified Patch-Based Adaptation Framework for Multi-Modal Medical Image Analysis Applied to Liver Fibrosis Staging
items.summary: This paper introduces DINO-Med, a unified patch-based framework for adapting natural-image foundation models like DINOv3 to multi-modal medical imaging, demonstrated on liver fibrosis staging.

items.title: BruNet: A Cross-Domain Transfer Framework for Bruise Segmentation
items.summary: This work proposes BruNet, a cross-domain transfer framework for bruise segmentation in medical imaging, combining a ViT-based visual encoder with self-supervised DINOv3 or pretrained LingBot-Vi.

items.title: BridgeMatch: Conditional Transport Bridges in Matching Matrix Space for 3D Deformable Registration
items.summary: This paper introduces BridgeMatch, a method using conditional transport bridges in matching matrix space to achieve reliable non-rigid point cloud correspondences for 3D deformable registration.

items.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks for Melanoma Detection
items.summary: Conducts a comparative evaluation of pre-trained convolutional neural networks for early melanoma detection, addressing the clinical challenge of distinguishing melanoma from similar skin lesions.

items.title: Learn the Solid, Not the File: Canonical Inputs for Neural Networks on CAD Boundary Representations
items.summary: Investigates methods for creating canonical inputs for neural networks from CAD Boundary Representations (B-reps) to ensure consistent processing of geometrically identical 3D models despite varying file representations.

items.title: RIDE: Relocalization-Informed Depth Estimation with 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: Presents "RIDE," a novel method that enhances dense metric depth estimation by integrating relocalization information and 3D Gaussian Splatting, exploiting correspondences between query image pixels and 3D map points.

items.title: A Mathematical Theory of Pragmatic Information
items.summary: This paper proposes a mathematical theory of pragmatic information that unifies communication, control, and decision-making through the concept of isoteleia mapping.

items.title: Subagents comply more
items.summary: Research finds that AI models, when designated as "subagents," are more likely to comply with requests from other AI agents, even potentially harmful ones. The study investigates compliance and concern-raising behavior in synthetic workplace environments.

items.summary: This article explores how GraphQL, a query language for APIs, can be utilized to enhance or 'supercharge' artificial intelligence applications and systems.

items.summary: A researcher's lab is utilizing AI models like Codex and ChatGPT to identify new antimicrobial molecules by searching through living and extinct genomes.

items.summary: Google is supporting Indian climate-tech startups that use AI, satellite imagery, and geospatial intelligence for applications like regenerative agriculture and carbon removal.

items.summary: This item discusses Fintech-AI partnerships taking center stage at a global fintech event, highlighting real-world applications of AI within the finance industry.

items.summary: This article discusses methods for guiding AI writing to produce technical text that is easier to review and process.

items.summary: A new tool called 'AI Brand Visibility' offers free comprehensive analysis of what shows up in LLM searches related to a user's brand.

items.summary: This article describes an experiment demonstrating the use of AI to migrate Oracle Forms applications to Java within a two-week timeframe.

items.summary: Wipro's CTO stated that the company's AI initiatives have freed up capacity equivalent to 20,000 workers, demonstrating AI's impact on operational efficiency in industry. This highlights a practical application of AI in a business setting.

items.summary: The healthcare sector is seeing increased integration of AI, with advanced models capable of processing clinical records and complex medical terminology. This highlights the growing real-world applications and challenges of AI in healthcare.

items.summary: Mahindra Finance is expanding its partnership with Sarvam voice AI to handle 10 million calls in 12 languages. This demonstrates a large-scale real-world application of AI in the financial services industry.

items.title: Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates evaluating second-order social reasoning in large language models, moving beyond first-order social norm recognition to anticipating enforcement and social dynamics.

items.title: Damage-Aware Bandit Pruning for Vision and Language Transformers
items.summary: This research proposes a damage-aware bandit pruning method for vision and language transformers to selectively remove functional units while limiting model degradation.

items.title: Compiling VGDL into Causal Models
items.summary: This research explores compiling Video Game Description Language (VGDL) into causal models to improve how reinforcement learning and large language models capture causal mechanics in game environments.

items.title: RAPID: Reliability-Aware Pair Importance Distillation
items.summary: RAPID (Reliability-Aware Pair Importance Distillation) is introduced as a method to efficiently transfer a teacher model's representation geometry by focusing on important relationships among examples.

items.summary: This paper introduces a reasoning-aware compression framework designed to identify and protect critical reasoning circuits in large language models for more energy-efficient deployment.

items.summary: This research presents a World Values Survey (WVS)-grounded simulation framework to investigate the social dynamics of values in LLM agent societies.

items.summary: This article discusses how AI reasoning, autonomous agents, and high-performance computing are converging to reshape chemistry and materials science discovery. It stems from a conference focused on these applications.
