items.summary: This research studies how Vision-Language Models (VLMs) maintain confidence and reliability when visual evidence is progressively degraded. It examines answer-level consistency in VLMs like Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instr under varying evidence loss.

items.title: Integrating Unimodal and Vision-Language Representations in Latent Space for Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification
items.summary: This study proposes a framework for multi-label chest X-ray classification that integrates unimodal and vision-language representations in a latent space. It combines visual representations from RAD-DINO with clinical semantic knowledge for improved diagnostic accuracy.

items.title: M2LG-DG: A Multi-modal Local-Global Domain Generalization Framework for Cross-site Major Depressive Disorder Classification
items.summary: This research proposes M2LG-DG, a multi-modal local-global domain generalization framework to improve the performance of Major Depressive Disorder classification models across different imaging sites. It addresses the issue of model performance degradation when applied to data from new clinical settings.

items.title: MLLMs Hallucinate when Information Distribution Drifts in Synergy Heads
items.summary: This research investigates hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), attributing them to information distribution drifts within synergy heads. The study aims to understand why MLLMs struggle with reliability in practical applications.

items.title: DensePol: Dense-Angle Polarization Dataset for Learning-Based Polarimetric Vision
items.summary: DensePol is introduced as a new dataset for learning-based polarimetric vision, providing dense-angle polarization data. This dataset aims to improve the fidelity of predicting polarization from conventional RGB images, offering physical cues about scene properties.

items.title: The Living Library: Transforming Archival Collections into Conversational Knowledge Systems -- Lessons from the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library
items.summary: The Living Library is an end-to-end framework that transforms fragmented digital archives into governed, conversational knowledge systems for in-person exhibit experiences. Developed at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, it facilitates interactive access to historical collections.

items.title: OmniPoint: Universal Monocular Metric Pointcloud from Any Camera
items.summary: OmniPoint is presented as a unified framework for generating universal monocular metric pointclouds from any camera. It aims to generalize metric 3D geometry reconstruction from monocular images, overcoming limitations of fixed camera model assumptions.

items.title: Vision-language models know more about agriculture than they show and rubric-grounded verifications close the gap
items.summary: This research explores the potential of Vision-language models (VLMs) for agricultural classification, finding that their knowledge often exceeds their zero-shot performance. The study proposes rubric-grounded verifications to improve VLM efficacy in identifying agricultural issues.

items.title: Low-Rank Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models with Fixed-Token Bases
items.summary: This research proposes Low-Rank Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) using fixed-token bases. It investigates adapting models like CLIP to downstream recognition tasks by optimizing continuous context vectors for prompt learning.

items.title: LeCor: Learning to Be Corrected by Meta-Learned Test-Time Training for Interactive 3D Lung-Tumour Segmentation
items.summary: LeCor introduces a method for interactive 3D lung-tumour segmentation where the model learns to be corrected by clinicians using meta-learned test-time training. This approach aims to streamline radiotherapy planning by enabling efficient refinement of AI-proposed contours.

items.title: Learning Global Camera Poses from Noisy View-Graphs for Structure from Motion
items.summary: This research introduces a deep, global Structure-from-Motion framework for learning camera poses from noisy view-graphs. The method utilizes a permutation-equivariant graph neural network to improve 3D reconstruction and view-synthesis.

items.title: MotionBlind: Probing the Illusion of Motion Understanding in Video-LLMs
items.summary: MotionBlind is a study that probes the limitations of Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) regarding their ability to understand motion. The research demonstrates that Video-LLMs often fail to accurately interpret dynamics like speed, direction, or force.

items.title: Hyperbolic Geometry for Open-World Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
items.summary: This research proposes using hyperbolic geometry to improve open-world object detection (OWOD) in remote sensing imagery. The approach aims to better represent latent hierarchical relationships among object categories, enhancing the identification of unknown objects.

items.title: LightMedSeg-ISLES: Stroke Lesion Segmentation with 81x Fewer Parameters than nnU-Net
items.summary: LightMedSeg-ISLES is introduced as a highly efficient pipeline for T1-weighted stroke lesion segmentation, operating with 81 times fewer parameters than nnU-Net. This system aims to reduce storage and inference demands for medical imaging deployment.

items.title: VFNet: Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Model for Void Fraction Estimation in Gas-Liquid Two-Phase Flow
items.summary: VFNet is introduced as a multi-view spatio-temporal model designed for accurate void fraction estimation in gas-liquid two-phase flow. This model aims to overcome limitations of existing methods by providing generalized estimations without relying on restrictive flow assumptions.

items.title: Freezing of Gait Prediction Under Spatial Occlusion: An IMU-Supervised Cross-Modal Distillation Approach
items.summary: This research proposes an IMU-supervised cross-modal distillation approach for automated freezing-of-gait detection in Parkinson's disease, aiming to improve objective assessment of motor impairment.

items.title: Layerwise Tunable Lifting Scheme for the Convolutional Neural Network
items.summary: This work introduces a family of tunable lifting schemes for biorthogonal wavelet filter banks, proposing three strategies to adapt low-pass, high-pass, or both frequency branches within convolutional neural networks.

items.title: SkNeXt enables topology-guided neuronal reconstruction from petabyte-scale microscopy data
items.summary: SkNeXt is presented as a method to enable topology-guided neuronal reconstruction from petabyte-scale microscopy data, addressing computational and data movement challenges in neuroscience imaging.

items.title: Pretraining and Distillation Matter More Than Architecture Family for Label-Free Single-Cell Classification
items.summary: This study compares deep learning architectures for label-free single-cell classification, concluding that pretraining and distillation are more critical factors than the specific architecture family (CNNs vs. transformers) for achieving performance.

items.title: From Pixels to Hierarchical Sequences: Quadtree Mask Encoding for Vision-Language Binary Change Detection
items.summary: This research introduces Quadtree Mask Encoding for Vision-Language Binary Change Detection in remote sensing, aiming to improve pixel-level mask generation by overcoming limitations of existing VLMs confined to change captioning or external decoders.

items.title: CLFTv2: Efficient Camera-LiDAR Fusion for Semantic Segmentation via Hierarchical Feature Pyramids
items.summary: CLFTv2 is introduced as an efficient camera-LiDAR fusion framework that uses hierarchical feature pyramids to enhance semantic segmentation for autonomous driving, particularly for detecting vulnerable road users.

items.title: Albedo Estimation via Latent Bridge Matching
items.summary: This research proposes "Latent Bridge Matching" for albedo estimation in Intrinsic Image Decomposition, addressing challenges like physical consistency, computational cost, and generalization limitations in current generative models.

items.title: Interpreting Object-Dependent Concept Brittleness in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
items.summary: This research identifies and interprets an object-dependent concept brittleness in text-to-image diffusion models, where specific objects consistently fail to realize intended concepts despite prompt-following abilities.

items.title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations via Class-Wise Adaptive Modality Fusion and Affective Geometry
items.summary: This work extends the Self-Distillation Transformer for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC), incorporating class-wise adaptive modality fusion and appearance+geometry visual representations to integrate heterogeneous cues effectively.

items.title: Vague2Detect: Handling Ambiguous Prompts in Knowledge-Based Open-World Detection
items.summary: Vague2Detect proposes a new approach to handle ambiguous prompts in knowledge-based open-world detection, aiming to overcome limitations of conventional and open-vocabulary models in interpreting vague language for object identification.

items.title: From Few-Shot Segmentation to Clinician-in-the-Loop Medical Image Analysis
items.summary: This work explores the limitations of standard few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) in real-world clinical settings, advocating for a "clinician-in-the-loop" approach to address issues like acquisition shift and atypical pathology.

items.title: What Makes Adversarial Examples Transfer Across Deepfake Detectors?
items.summary: This research investigates the mechanisms behind the transferability of adversarial examples across deepfake detectors in black-box attacks, aiming to understand how source-target compatibility influences attack success.

items.title: Beyond Similarity: Foundation Models as an Efficient Backbone for Training-Free Composed Video Retrieval
items.summary: This research proposes using foundation models as an efficient backbone for training-free composed video retrieval (CoVR), addressing the challenge of maintaining both efficient search and the ability to capture transient video actions.

items.title: Elastoformer: Enabling Dynamic Adaptivity via Elastic Model Transformation
items.summary: Elastoformer introduces a method for dynamic adaptivity in EdgeAI systems, enabling Deep Neural Networks to adjust to fluctuating constraints on latency, power, and memory resources through elastic model transformation.

items.title: TransGaze-Object: Transformer Based Driver Gaze Object Prediction Framework in Real Driving
items.summary: TransGaze-Object proposes a Transformer-based framework for predicting driver gaze objects in real-driving scenarios, offering more semantically rich object-level gaze information compared to traditional gaze zone or point-of-gaze methods.

items.title: 3rd Place Solution to Human Motion Challenges in Real-World and Clinical Settings (MoCha) @ECCV2026: Language-Aligned Motion Representations for Domain-Generalizable UPDRS-Gait Severity Estimation
items.summary: This work presents a 3rd place solution to human motion challenges, introducing language-aligned motion representations for domain-generalizable UPDRS-Gait severity estimation, utilizing a Bi-GRU backbone to learn semantically structured motion features.

items.title: UOT-Gap: A Variational Principle for the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models via Unbalanced Optimal Transport
items.summary: This paper presents a variational principle for understanding the modality gap in vision-language models like CLIP, where image and text distributions often remain separated. It connects this gap to initialization, contrastive dynamics, and information imbalance.

items.title: When Fusion Fails: Corruption-Aware Rebalanced Fusion for Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: This research addresses the challenge of multi-modal medical image segmentation where fusion of diagnostic information can fail due to differing input quality. It proposes a corruption-aware rebalanced fusion method to improve performance.

items.title: FreqFLD: Towards All-in-One Facial Landmark Detection via Frequency Modulation
items.summary: This paper introduces FreqFLD, a new method for facial landmark detection that uses frequency modulation. It aims to provide an all-in-one solution by processing features in a geometry-driven manner, unlike most existing spatial-domain methods.

items.title: Isotropic Embedding Perturbations for Robust Vision Language Encoders
items.summary: This research explores isotropic embedding perturbations as a data augmentation technique to enhance the robustness of vision-language encoders and other deep multimodal models. It aims to overcome performance saturation seen with combined existing augmentation methods.

items.title: SynThermFace: Amplifying Limited Paired Data for Visible-Thermal Face Recognition via Synthetic Data Generation
items.summary: This paper proposes SynThermFace, a method to amplify limited paired data for visible-thermal face recognition using synthetic data generation. This addresses the degradation of conventional face recognition models when high-quality RGB images are unavailable.

items.title: JEPA Policy: Diffusion-Free Imitation Learning via Paired Action and Future Representation Prediction
items.summary: This paper presents JEPA Policy, a diffusion-free imitation learning framework that uses paired action and future representation prediction. It aims to improve upon standard behavior cloning by explicitly constraining the future representation associated with action chunks.

items.summary: A lung drug discovered using AI has demonstrated the ability to reverse markers of aging in a recent study.

items.title: LLM retrospective preferences can diverge from turn-by-turn state ratings
items.summary: A study found that retrospective preferences of LLMs, like Llama-3.1-70B, can change based on conversation endings and do not consistently align with turn-by-turn or final state ratings, suggesting a complex preference mechanism.

items.title: Anthropic AI 'formalizes' proof of Fermat's last theorem in just 11 days
items.summary: Anthropic AI has successfully formalized a proof of Fermat's last theorem in just 11 days, showcasing an application of AI in scientific and mathematical research.

items.title: Actually Real AI
items.summary: Actually Real AI is a project by Arthur focused on creating interactive AI art installations that aim for more human-like interactions. It explores the application of AI in creative and experiential contexts.

items.title: Code Reviews in the Age of AI
items.summary: This article discusses the implications and methods of conducting code reviews in the era of artificial intelligence. It explores how AI can be integrated into the code review process.

items.title: El Yayster – a resident LLM that inhabits Emacs
items.summary: El Yayster is an integration that allows a large language model (LLM) to operate as a resident component within the Emacs text editor. It provides LLM capabilities directly within the Emacs environment.

items.title: Revise AI, an AI editor for fiction writers
items.summary: Revise AI is an application designed to assist fiction writers with editing their work. It functions as an AI-powered editor to enhance writing.

items.title: AI-designed drug appears to turn back the body's biological clock in early trial
items.summary: An AI-designed drug, rentosertib, by Insilico Medicine, shows early trial results suggesting it can reverse biological aging markers in patients.

items.title: Unsupervised Feature Discovery via Simple Clustering
items.summary: This abstract explores whether clustering methods can effectively discover interpretable and useful features within the activation space of AI models, specifically Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

items.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
items.summary: Early data suggests an AI-developed drug candidate, rentosertib, for a rare lung condition could also slow biological signs of aging.

items.title: Best AI Tools for Turning Long Videos into YouTube Shorts in 2026
items.summary: This article discusses the best AI tools available for transforming long videos into YouTube Shorts, focusing on practical applications of AI in content creation.

items.title: How AI wiped out an entire industry in Nairobi
items.summary: The article describes how ChatGPT, an AI model, has led to the demise of an academic paper writing industry in Nairobi, illustrating a significant real-world application and impact of AI on a business sector.

items.title: Show HN: Neuro, a compiled language for AI that matches Clang -O2
items.summary: Neuro is introduced as a new compiled language designed for AI development, claiming to match the performance of Clang -O2.

items.title: Show HN: A brainstorm canvas with no back end, running on Chrome's on-device AI
items.summary: A new brainstorm canvas application is presented, which operates without a backend and leverages Chrome's on-device AI capabilities.

items.title: Who else is steering?
items.summary: A post raises a methodological question about understanding AI models' behaviors in response to activation steering, specifically focusing on introspection.

items.title: Data-Optimized Contingency Screening: A Machine Learning Approach to Power System Security
items.summary: This study investigates a machine learning approach for data-optimized contingency screening to enhance power system security, enabling proactive decision-making and mitigating large-scale disruptions.

items.title: BioSync: Transformer-Based Cross-Modal Fusion for a Multimodal Physiological Digital Biomarker
items.summary: BioSync introduces a Transformer-based cross-modal fusion method to combine physiological measurements from wearable devices into the BioSync Index (BSI), a continuous composite digital biomarker.

items.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Composition-Dependent Constitutive Models for Hyperelasticity and Viscoelasticity of Digital Materials
items.summary: This research describes a data-driven method to discover composition-dependent constitutive models for the hyperelasticity and viscoelasticity of digital materials. These materials are fabricated by multi-material 3D printing.

items.title: From Answers to Interpretations: Rethinking Ambiguity-Induced Aleatoric Uncertainty Estimation in LLMs
items.summary: This research rethinks the estimation of ambiguity-induced aleatoric uncertainty in LLMs, a challenge for reliable deployment. It aims to distinguish between uncertainty from inherent task variability and limitations in the model's knowledge.

items.title: Reducing Hallucinated Transcripts in Whisper via Hallucination Space Projection
items.summary: This research proposes a training-free, inference-time method called "hallucination space projection" to reduce hallucinated transcripts produced by the Whisper automatic speech recognition model. The method addresses fluent but incorrect outputs from Whisper's generative decoder.

items.title: Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability
items.summary: This research investigates how extremely sparse supervision can incentivize reasoning abilities in large language models, challenging the assumption that effective learning requires massive numbers of tokens. It explores new approaches to LLM post-training.

items.title: Leveraging Imperfect Restoration for Data Availability Attack
items.summary: This research proposes a Data Availability Attack (DAA) that leverages imperfect restoration to make online data unlearnable for deep learning models. The method aims to prevent unauthorized usage of data by subtly perturbing training data.

items.title: Predicting Spatiotemporal Mobile Sensing-Based PM2.5 Concentrations Using Low-Rank Adapted Spatially Attentive Graph Neural Network
items.summary: This research introduces a low-rank adapted spatially attentive Graph Neural Network to predict spatiotemporal PM2.5 concentrations based on mobile sensing data. It also presents a novel mobile-sensing dataset from Surat, India, for urban air quality monitoring.

items.title: Model Retirement Creates Reproducibility Risk in Biomedical AI Publications
items.summary: This research highlights the risk to scientific reproducibility in biomedical AI publications due to the retirement and deprecation schedules of large language models hosted by commercial services. It examines the implications for scientific integrity.

items.title: PLUME: Parameter-Efficient Personalization of Large Language Models via Low-Rank User Modulation in Shared Subspaces
items.summary: PLUME is a method for parameter-efficient personalization of large language models using low-rank user modulation in shared subspaces. It aims to achieve high-quality individual personalization without incurring significant parameter and storage overhead.

items.title: AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems
items.summary: AutoLR describes a process at NetEase's gaming-community app for automating the path from research to launch review in industrial recommender systems, streamlining the iterative development and deployment of algorithms.

items.title: A Data Fusion Framework for Grounding Aerospace Surrogate Model via Experimental Wind-Tunnel Observations
items.summary: This research presents a data fusion framework to improve the predictive fidelity of aerospace surrogate models by integrating experimental wind-tunnel observations with high-fidelity CFD data.

items.title: Quantum-Assisted Memory-Efficient Training for Parameter-Intensive Wi-Fi-Based Human Activity Recognition
items.summary: This study proposes a quantum-assisted, memory-efficient training method for parameter-intensive deep learning models used in Wi-Fi-based human activity recognition, addressing their computational and memory demands.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Forced Outage Risk Prediction: Benefits and Comparison to Machine Learning
items.summary: This study evaluates the capability of large language models to predict weather-related forced outages in power grids using a zero-shot framework and compares their performance to traditional machine learning methods.

items.title: Data-Driven Learning of Unknown Nonlinear Differential Equations Using Functional Analysis
items.summary: This paper proposes a new interpretable machine learning method for the data-driven discovery of unknown nonlinear ordinary differential equations, learning the underlying vector field without prior system knowledge.

items.title: Modular Deep Recurrent Neural Network: Application to Quadrotors
items.summary: This work introduces a modular deep Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) designed to simplify the deployment of various RNN architectures and automate derivative computation for gradient-based learning, demonstrating its application to quadrotors.

items.title: A Quantum Variational Approach to Prototypical Recurrent Unit
items.summary: This paper introduces a lightweight Quantum Prototypical Recurrent Unit (QPRU) using a quantum variational approach, requiring significantly fewer parameters than classical and other quantum recurrent architectures.

items.title: Disentangling Attention in Deep Operator Learning: A Controlled Study of Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Architectures
items.summary: This study conducts a controlled analysis of attention mechanisms within deep neural operators, examining their role in learning mappings between input functions and PDE solution fields in both data-driven and physics-informed architectures.

items.title: REFINE: LLM Refinement over Budgeted Text-Attributed Graphs for Personalized Medical Concept Representation
items.summary: This paper introduces REFINE, an LLM refinement method applied over budgeted text-attributed graphs to learn personalized medical concept representations for improved EHR prediction.

items.title: A Repeated-Measurement Study for Cultural Analytics of English Song Lyrics Using Five Large Language Models
items.summary: This repeated-measurement study evaluates the reliability of five large language models for annotating cultural texts in the context of cultural analytics of English song lyrics.

items.title: When Load-Balancing Goes Too Far: Expert Pruning in Over-Dispersed Mixture-of-Experts Models
items.summary: This paper investigates how expert pruning in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models can fail under over-dispersed routing, revealing that router probabilities become unreliable for identifying low-importance experts in such scenarios.

items.title: On-board ML for Trace Gas detection in Imaging Spectroscopy data
items.summary: This work explores using on-board machine learning for real-time trace gas detection in imaging spectroscopy data, aiming to overcome the delays of ground-based processing for environmental monitoring.

items.title: Nested Inductive Bias Framework for SPD Manifold Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes a Nested Inductive Bias Framework for Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) manifold learning in Geometric Deep Learning, addressing both manifold constraints and relational priors.

items.title: Hakken: Predicting future discoveries to fill the gaps in today's knowledge
items.summary: This paper presents Hakken, a domain-agnostic system that uses a transformer-based model to predict and explain novel scientific discoveries by identifying new relationships beyond existing knowledge.

items.title: An Energy-Based Conservative-Dissipative Latent Neural Evolution Operator for Magnetization Dynamics
items.summary: This research develops an energy-based reduced-order model for micromagnetic magnetization dynamics, coupling a convolutional autoencoder with a structured latent neural ordinary differential equation.

items.title: Training-Free Halving of Activated Experts in Fine-Grained Mixture-of-Experts Models
items.summary: This paper presents a training-free method to halve the number of activated experts in fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by adjusting router probabilities, thereby enhancing inference efficiency.

items.title: GNN-Guided Graph Coarsening and Adaptive QUBO Penalties for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows on a Quantum Annealer
items.summary: This paper proposes a GNN-guided graph coarsening method and adaptive QUBO penalties to reduce the problem size for solving capacitated vehicle routing problems with time windows on a quantum annealer. The method merges nearby customers into super-nodes to simplify the problem formulation.

items.title: Too Rare to Learn: Prescribed Cyclone Tracks Degrade a Bay of Bengal Ocean Emulator
items.summary: This research investigates the use of neural ocean emulators for regional forecasting in cyclone-exposed coastal seas, finding that prescribing cyclone tracks as input can degrade performance in the Bay of Bengal. The study highlights challenges in training these models with rare events.

items.title: SMILE: Bridging Continuous Optimization and Discrete Symbolic Recovery
items.summary: This paper introduces SMILE, a new method designed to improve symbolic regression by bridging continuous optimization and discrete symbolic recovery to discover closed-form mathematical expressions from data. It aims to address issues of slow convergence and lack of compositional structure exploitation in existing methods.

items.title: Interpretability for Turing Machines
items.summary: This research applies susceptibilities, an interpretability technique developed for neural networks, to Turing machines to identify the presence of algorithmic structure. It probes the local loss landscape of a learning problem for noisy Turing machines.

items.title: WEECFP-SuRGE: Wide Embedded Extended Connectivity Fingerprint with Substructure Rotary Graph-distance Encoding
items.summary: This paper introduces WEECFP, a parameter-free 1024-dimensional continuous molecular fingerprint, and WEECFP-SuRGE, a transformer architecture that applies Substructure Rotary Graph-distance Encoding (SuRGE) in its self-attention mechanism. These methods aim to improve molecular representation for AI models.

items.title: Locating and Steering Refusal Beyond Attention
items.summary: This research investigates the internal mechanisms of language models to locate and steer refusal behaviors, examining how these mechanisms differ between transformer and state-space models. The findings contribute to safety and interpretability tooling by pinpointing where refusal is governed within the model architecture.

items.title: Training Large Language Models for Small-Molecule Design with Synthetic Task Scaling
items.summary: This paper explores training large language models (LLMs) for small-molecule design using synthetic task scaling to efficiently search for viable drug candidates. It leverages LLMs' generative capabilities and representational capacity for navigating complex chemical spaces.

items.title: A Robust Watermark-based Fingerprint Framework for GNNs Ownership Verification
items.summary: This paper introduces a robust watermark-based fingerprint framework for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to verify model ownership and prevent intellectual property infringement like model stealing. The method addresses concerns regarding the high training costs and unauthorized misuse of GNNs.

items.title: Dynamic Heterogeneous Graph Representation Learning: A Survey
items.summary: This paper provides a survey of dynamic heterogeneous graph representation learning, addressing the challenges of modeling evolving heterogeneous entities and complex interactions in real-world AI systems. It serves as a canonical paradigm for modeling complex networks.

items.title: How Faithful Is Attribution for Sales Forecasting? A Counterfactual Study
items.summary: This counterfactual study evaluates the faithfulness of attribution methods for deep models in sales forecasting, which are typically opaque despite their accuracy. The researchers propose adding a post-hoc, architecture-agnostic interpretability layer to enhance transparency.

items.title: Federated Attack Campaign Detection via Contrastive Encoding of Threat Indicators in Gradient Updates
items.summary: This research proposes a method for federated attack campaign detection using contrastive encoding of threat indicators within gradient updates, leveraging federated learning to overcome data sharing barriers between organizations. This enables training shared threat detectors without centralizing sensitive telemetry.

items.title: PACE: Propagation-Aware Collaborative Correction for One-Shot Personalized Federated Graph Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces PACE, a method for Propagation-Aware Collaborative Correction in one-shot personalized federated graph learning, addressing challenges arising from client heterogeneity. It aims to balance the benefits of knowledge transfer from other subgraphs with the risks of incompatible information.

items.title: When Genomic Masking Priors Fail to Transfer: Strong Variant Prediction, Weak Functional Generation
items.summary: This research investigates the transferability of genomic masking priors and introduces GenDA (Genomic Density-optimized Absorbing Diffusion), a bidirectional discrete diffusion model for genomic modeling. It aims to reconstruct missing sequences and improve functional generation in genomics.

items.title: From Deep to Shallow: Unconstrained and Efficient Layer Merging Strategy
items.summary: This paper proposes an unconstrained and efficient layer merging strategy for deep neural networks to reduce their computational demands, making them more applicable in resource-constrained environments. This method focuses on depth compression by identifying and linearizing redundant activation functions.

items.title: Adaptation Interfaces for In-Context Tabular Foundation Models in Time-to-Event Prediction
items.summary: This research explores adaptation interfaces for in-context tabular foundation models to extend their capabilities to censored time-to-event prediction. It addresses the challenges of handling censoring and event-time dynamics in applying these models to structured data.

items.title: Physics-Aware Random Walk Fingerprints for Scalable Power Grid Graph Classification
items.summary: This paper introduces physics-aware random walk fingerprints for scalable power grid graph classification, aiming to improve predictive performance on tasks like cascading-failure classification. It provides an alternative to end-to-end training and model-specific tuning typically required by graph neural networks.

items.title: Fractal basins trap latent reasoning
items.summary: This research investigates the mechanisms of reasoning in artificial intelligence models, proposing that "fractal basins" can trap latent reasoning. It explores how these models revisit and correct mistakes, which is fundamental to advancements in areas like mathematical theorem solving and autonomous task planning.

items.title: Solution-space heterogeneity shapes federated learning dynamics across partial differential equations
items.summary: This research explores how heterogeneity in solution spaces influences federated learning dynamics for training neural surrogates across partial differential equations. It addresses challenges in defining non-independent and identically distributed data in such settings.

items.title: Amortizing Scaling Law Construction Costs
items.summary: This paper proposes methods to amortize the computational costs associated with constructing scaling laws for large foundation models. It aims to make the derivation of these design guides more efficient than exhaustive grid training.

items.title: Confounding-Valid Conformal Inference for Counterfactual KPIs in Wireless Networks
items.summary: This research introduces confounding-valid conformal inference to enable wireless network operators to reliably answer counterfactual "what-if" questions about network operation. It uses logged telemetry to generate prediction sets for key performance indicators (KPIs).

items.title: Deep Microcompression: Structured Pruning and Bit-packed Quantization for Microcontrollers
items.summary: This paper introduces Deep Microcompression (DMC), a hardware-aware pipeline for deep learning inference on bare-metal microcontrollers. DMC integrates structured pruning, quantization-aware training, and bit-packing to achieve significant weight compression.

items.title: Evidence Integration in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates how large language models integrate external evidence supplied by tools, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, and users. It proposes a distributional theory to explain this evidence integration process.

items.title: MedProb: Probing Internal Representations of Vision-Language Models for Medical Question Answering
items.summary: MedProb is introduced as a lightweight probing framework that predicts multiple-choice Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) answers directly from frozen Vision-Language Model representations. It aims to revisit assumptions about Med-VQA requirements.

items.title: VERGE: Verification-Enhanced Refinement for Grounded Extraction of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Symptoms in Clinical Notes
items.summary: This paper introduces VERGE, a verification-enhanced refinement system for grounded extraction of early-onset colorectal cancer symptoms from clinical notes. The goal is to support early detection and inform follow-up for this increasing condition.

items.title: The Anatomy of an ASR Hallucination
items.summary: This research analyzes the anatomy of ASR hallucinations, where systems produce fluent but unrelated text, viewing them as a consequence of grounding failure. It investigates where this failure becomes possible within the system.

items.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Cross-Lingual Consistency Enhancement Methods in Multilingual Language Models
items.summary: This paper presents a systematic evaluation of various methods designed to enhance cross-lingual consistency in multilingual language models. It addresses the issue of models producing inconsistent answers to semantically equivalent questions across languages.

items.title: What Attention Recalls and Recurrence Controls in Hybrid Language Models
items.summary: This research investigates the distinct roles of attention and recurrence in hybrid language models, introducing cache-level interventions like split-prefill. It aims to clarify what each mechanism recalls and controls within the models.

items.title: Shared circuits predict whether LLMs generalize across formats in arithmetic reasoning
items.summary: This research investigates whether large language models generalize across different input formats in arithmetic reasoning, a capability effortless for humans but brittle for LLMs. It aims to identify shared circuits that predict this generalization.

items.title: Patterns of Priming in Production: Lexical, Semantic and Structural Alignment in Language Model Generation
items.summary: This paper investigates patterns of structural priming in language model generation, examining how preceding structural context influences sentence completion. It explores lexical, semantic, and structural alignment in LM production.

items.title: Cultural Misalignment in Large Language Models: Detection, Measurement, and Mitigation Through Targeted Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This research evaluates open-weight LLMs (Gemma3-12B, Bielik-11B-v3, Qwen3-4B) for cultural misalignment using World Values Survey data across different demographics and countries. It proposes a targeted fine-tuning method to detect, measure, and mitigate this misalignment.

items.title: Towards Understanding Pause Token Fine-Tuning Dynamics: A Mode Retention Perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates the training dynamics of pause-token methods, which are used to improve LLM reasoning by inserting special tokens into sequences. It explores how these tokens reshape training dynamics from a mode retention perspective.

items.title: LentEx: Generalizable Latent Entity Extraction via Synthetic Data and Instruction-Tuned LLMs
items.summary: This paper introduces LentEx, a novel framework for latent entity extraction that leverages synthetic data and instruction-tuned LLMs. It aims to identify implicit, contextually inferred entities within free text, an area where traditional methods often fall short.

items.title: Scale-QLoRA: Code-Invariant Adapter Merging for Native 4-bit Microscaling LLMs
items.summary: This paper proposes a method for code-invariant adapter merging in native 4-bit microscaling LLMs, known as Scale-QLoRA. It addresses the challenges of merging LoRA adapters into base models for deployment efficiency without per-forward overhead.

items.title: A Calibrated Reflection Approach for Enhancing Confidence Estimation in LLMs
items.summary: This paper presents a 'Calibrated Reflection' approach designed to enhance confidence estimation in large language models. The goal is to provide reliable mechanisms for LLMs to determine when to trust their outputs or seek human intervention.

items.title: When Do Internal Probes Beat Reading the Answer? Miscalibrated Readouts and Behavior-Concealed Knowledge in Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates how internal probes can reveal knowledge concealed within language models, even when their external behavior appears miscalibrated. It uses linear probes on hidden states to accurately assess a model's understanding.

items.title: Tracing Audio Grounding and Answer Selection in Audio LLMs
items.summary: This paper investigates how Audio Large Language Models process information, specifically tracing whether their answer selection is based on actual audio grounding or textual cues. It addresses the challenge of ensuring models reason from provided audio rather than linguistic priors.

items.title: Choosing the Right Language Mode at Inference Time for Multilingual Reliability
items.summary: This research investigates how to improve multilingual large language models' reasoning capabilities, especially in low- to mid-resource languages. It explores the role of translation at inference time to access stronger English-centric representations.

items.title: Controlling and Assessing Appropriate Persona Use in LLM-based Dialogue Generation
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of controlling and assessing appropriate persona use in LLM-based dialogue generation. It investigates why LLMs overuse persona attributes and aims to develop methods to mitigate this issue and metrics for evaluation.

items.title: How Do Language Models Represent and Use Phonological Information for Allomorph Selection?
items.summary: This research investigates how language models represent and utilize phonological information for allomorph selection, despite being trained on tokenized text. It explores whether they rely on memorization or rule-like generalization for phonologically conditioned morphemes.

items.title: Beneath the Surface of Chains-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning Operations in LLMs
items.summary: This paper provides a mechanistic interpretation of reasoning operations in large language models using Chains-of-Thought. It explores how diverse functional operations, such as problem formulation and deduction, are geometrically organized within representation spaces.

items.title: Vectorizing Classical Tamil: Representation Learning for Verse-Commentary Pairs
items.summary: This paper details the construction of a corpus of 1,262 Classical Tamil verse-commentary pairs and the application of representation learning techniques to it. It trains recurrent and Transformer encoders to recover information from the structured text.

items.title: Can Activation Steering Capture Multidimensional Authorship Style?
items.summary: This research investigates whether activation steering can effectively control large language model generation to capture multidimensional authorship style. It questions its ability to handle complex and hard-to-define attributes of writing.

items.title: Recurrence Is Not Enough: Causally Validating Multilingual SAE Translation Features in Gemma 2 and 3
items.summary: This paper causally validates multilingual Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) translation features in models like Gemma 2 and 3. It investigates whether features found in one language context play the same causal role when processing prompts in another language.

items.title: A Systematic Comparison of Multilingual Interpretability Methods Reveals Anisotropy-Driven Failures
items.summary: This paper systematically compares different interpretability methods for multilingual language models, revealing their limitations and disagreements in quantifying shared cross-lingual representations.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning for improving Large Language Models' Catalan text simplification capabilities
items.summary: This research investigates using reinforcement learning to enhance large language models' capabilities in automatic text simplification for low-resource languages like Catalan.

items.title: Generating Constructive Feedback on Stories via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper explores the application of reinforcement learning to large language models for generating constructive feedback on creative writing, aiming to provide a scalable and efficient alternative to human expert review.

items.title: CC-Mediation: Evaluating Large Language Models for Cross-Cultural Conflict Mediation
items.summary: This research investigates the challenges of evaluating large language models for cross-cultural conflict mediation, highlighting the need for specific mediation datasets and principled metrics to assess their effectiveness.

items.title: EuroAlpaca: Task-Preserving Localisation of Instruction Data for European Languages
items.summary: This paper introduces EuroAlpaca, a method for task-preserving localization of English instruction-tuning data into various European languages, addressing the issue of machine translation distorting task-critical constraints.

items.title: Influence Score and Transformers interpretability: Measure of the Effective Impact of Attention Heads at inference time
items.summary: This paper proposes an "influence score" as a new method to quantify the effective impact of attention heads on classification decisions in Transformer models, enhancing their interpretability during inference.

items.title: Improving Language Identification for Code-Switched Utterances with Integer Linear Programming
items.summary: This paper proposes an improved method using Integer Linear Programming to enhance language identification for code-switched utterances, addressing challenges in language identification (LID) systems.

items.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for AI-Assisted Scoring in Large-Scale Writing Assessment
items.summary: This study presents a human-in-the-loop framework for AI-assisted scoring in large-scale writing assessments, leveraging large language models to enhance the efficiency and scalability of grading processes.

items.title: From Vision to Language: Investigating Causal Information Flow in Multimodal Decision-Making
items.summary: This research investigates the causal information flow within Vision-Language Models to understand how visual evidence contributes to language-based decisions and cross-modal information processing.

items.title: Can Large Language Models Anticipate Behavioral Responses to Social Policies? A Case of Pension Enrollment Prediction among China's Flexible Workers
items.summary: This research explores using Large Language Models (LLMs) to anticipate behavioral responses to social policies, specifically for predicting pension enrollment among China's flexible workers. It proposes LLMs as a method to assess policy impacts, addressing challenges with traditional econometric methods.

items.title: A Verifier-Guided Explainable Reasoning Framework with Gold-Anchored QLoRA, Task-Aware Mixture-of-Experts, and Group-Relative RLVR
items.summary: This paper proposes a verifier-guided explainable reasoning framework for Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance transparency in educational question answering. The framework combines techniques like gold-anchored QLoRA, task-aware Mixture-of-Experts, and Group-Relative RLVR.

items.title: Step Back to Move Forward: Reflection-Aware Preference Optimization for Visual Generation
items.summary: This research proposes a reflection-aware preference optimization method using reinforcement learning to better align diffusion models for visual generation (text-to-image and text-to-video) with human preferences. The paper aims to improve the quality of multimedia content synthesis.

items.title: Joint Alignment and Distillation for Video Generation via Sample-Guided Distribution Matching
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for joint alignment and distillation for video generative models, using sample-guided distribution matching to align them with human preferences. This approach aims to reduce the computational overhead typically associated with Reinforcement Learning in such tasks.

items.title: Object Concepts Emerge from Motion
items.summary: This research presents a biologically inspired framework for learning object-centric visual representations, demonstrating how object concepts can emerge from motion. The goal is to improve physical-world perception by preserving the identity and coherence of individual instances in visual pretraining.

items.title: AdaptVPR: Route-Aware Hard Positive Generation for Robust Visual Place Recognition
items.summary: This research introduces AdaptVPR, a method for route-aware hard positive generation aimed at improving the robustness of Visual Place Recognition (VPR). It addresses the degradation of VPR performance caused by domain shifts like illumination, weather, and seasonal changes.

items.title: Where Appearance Fails, Geometry Recognizes: A CAD-Free 3D Shape Prior That Complements Vision Foundation Models
items.summary: This research proposes a CAD-Free 3D Shape Prior designed to complement Vision Foundation Models for object recognition, particularly in manufacturing and service robotics. It offers an alternative to conventional CAD models when labeled training sets are unavailable.

items.title: What Moves? Localized Motion Representations for Compositional Scene Control
items.summary: This research focuses on developing localized motion representations for compositional scene control, aiming to capture distinct motion patterns of individual entities within a shared scene. It addresses the limitation of existing video representations that encode motion globally.

items.title: FAVE: Foveated Adaptive Visual Encoding for Efficient Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
items.summary: This research introduces FAVE (Foveated Adaptive Visual Encoding), a method for efficient fine-grained visual understanding inspired by human active vision. It addresses the trade-off in visual encoders between high-resolution processing and compact global encoding to focus on local detail.

items.title: Topology-Aware Training and Spatial Diagnostics for Fiber Bundle Segmentation in Tracer Histology
items.summary: This research proposes topology-aware training and spatial diagnostics for fiber bundle segmentation in tracer histology, aiding in the analysis of axon bundle projections in the brain. The method provides anatomical reference information for validating diffusion MRI tractography.

items.title: DART: Depth-as-Target Pretraining for Surgical Vision Foundation Models
items.summary: This research proposes DART (Depth-as-Target Pretraining) for Surgical Vision Foundation Models, leveraging depth information in data-scarce domains like surgery. It aims to provide richer representations for downstream tasks compared to RGB-only pretraining.

items.title: Importance-Aware Low-Rank Distillation of Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: This research proposes Importance-Aware Low-Rank Distillation to make Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) more efficient for deployment in high-quality text-to-image generation. The method addresses the challenges posed by the scale of DiTs through parameter reduction.

items.title: ReaDiT Guidance: Control for Image and Video Generation using Diffusion Transformer Features
items.summary: This paper introduces ReaDiT Guidance, a lightweight framework for controlling image and video generation using Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models. It steers the generative process by leveraging DiT's internal feature representations according to spatial targets.

items.title: Retinal OCTA Phenotyping with LLM Reporting for Alzheimer's Disease
items.summary: This research explores using Retinal OCTA phenotyping combined with Large Language Model (LLM) reporting for the early identification of Alzheimer's Disease. It aims to develop a less costly and more suitable method for population-scale screening.

items.title: Enhancing Multimodal Emotion Recognition via Multi-Feature Encoding and Attention-Based Fusion
items.summary: This paper proposes a new multimodal emotion recognition framework that integrates rich audio and visual feature extraction with an attention-based fusion for improved performance in human-computer interaction. It addresses the growing interest in understanding emotions from multiple sensory inputs.

items.title: LookThere! Sparse Vision by Reinforced Selection
items.summary: This research introduces a method called "Sparse Vision by Reinforced Selection" to improve the efficiency of vision transformers by adaptively choosing which image tokens to process. It aims to accelerate inference while maintaining performance, especially at extreme sparsity.

items.title: AngelFingerprint: A Traceable, Explainable, and White-Box Stealthy Watermark for Text-Guided Image Editing
items.summary: AngelFingerprint introduces a new traceable, explainable, and stealthy watermark designed for images generated by text-guided diffusion models to ensure reliable provenance. It helps address disinformation concerns by explaining what changes were made and which prompt produced the image, even under white-box access.

items.title: HiSfM: Disambiguating Structure-from-Motion via Scaffold-Anchored Hierarchical Reconstruction
items.summary: HiSfM proposes a new method to disambiguate Structure-from-Motion (SfM) by using scaffold-anchored hierarchical reconstruction to improve 3D reconstruction. This advancement helps overcome challenges posed by visual ambiguity from repeated or symmetric structures in robotics and vision applications.

items.title: Bridging Modalities and Tasks: A Unified Hierarchical ViT for SAR-to-Optical Translation and Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: This research introduces a unified hierarchical Vision Transformer (ViT) that bridges modalities and tasks for SAR-to-optical translation and semantic segmentation. It aims to improve the interpretability of SAR images by converting them to optical images and performing semantic analysis.

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Learning Influential Views for VLM-based 3D Visual Grounding
items.summary: This paper explores learning influential camera views for Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based 3D visual grounding to more effectively localize objects in 3D scenes from natural language queries. It addresses limitations of existing methods that rely on heuristic rules for view selection.

items.title: SeamFlow: Structure-Aware Flow Matching on Edge Probabilities for Artist-Like UV Unwrapping
items.summary: SeamFlow introduces a new method for 3D surface cutting and UV unwrapping using structure-aware flow matching on edge probabilities, aiming for artist-like seam layouts. It seeks to improve visual semantic coherence beyond traditional geometric optimization or autoregressive generative methods.

items.title: LUMIN: Lightweight Universal Manufacturing Inspection Network for Anomaly Detection
items.summary: LUMIN presents a lightweight universal manufacturing inspection network designed for efficient anomaly detection in industrial settings. It tackles engineering bottlenecks related to memory bank construction latency and inference efficiency by optimizing sampling algorithms.

items.title: CLON: Cue-Calibrated Linguistic Object Onboarding for Zero-Shot 6D Pose Front-Ends
items.summary: CLON introduces Cue-Calibrated Linguistic Object Onboarding to enhance zero-shot 6D pose estimation front-ends by generating more accurate object proposals. This method aims to preserve true positives while effectively rejecting semantically plausible distractors.

items.title: An Attention-Guided Global and Local Fusion Framework for Lesion-Focused Image Classification
items.summary: This paper proposes an attention-guided global and local fusion framework for lesion-focused image classification to address challenges where discriminative signals are sparse and obscured by noise. The framework aims to improve the relevance of signals compared to uniform processing by conventional CNNs.

items.title: Intrinsic Temporal Adaptation of CLIP for Partially Relevant Video Retrieval
items.summary: This research introduces an intrinsic temporal adaptation of CLIP to improve Partially Relevant Video Retrieval (PRVR) by enabling fine-grained understanding of video moments relevant to a text query. It addresses the challenge of identifying relevant segments within untrimmed videos.

items.title: Weather-Conditioned Depth Anything
items.summary: This research introduces "Weather-Conditioned Depth Anything," an adaptation of monocular depth estimation foundation models to perform robustly under adverse weather conditions like fog, rain, and snow. It aims to overcome critical failures observed in current models in challenging environments.

items.title: PAPT++: Risk-Aware Adversarial Tuning and Generation for Single Domain Generalization
items.summary: PAPT++ introduces a risk-aware adversarial tuning and generation framework to enhance single domain generalization by enriching the source distribution with augmented or generated samples. It leverages text-to-image diffusion models to improve model performance on unseen target domains.

items.title: LetOccVote: Learning Weakly Supervised 3D Occupancy through Consensus
items.summary: LetOccVote proposes a method for learning weakly supervised 3D occupancy prediction through consensus, reducing reliance on costly 3D annotations by leveraging imperfect 2D pseudo-labels from vision foundation models. It aims to mitigate errors arising from direct use of imperfect supervision.

items.title: Mitigating Performance Discrepancy in Cross-Domain 3D Class-Incremental Learning
items.summary: This research focuses on mitigating performance discrepancies in cross-domain 3D class-incremental learning, which is critical for 3D perception models in applications like autonomous driving and robotics. It aims to enable models to continually adapt to newly emerging 3D object categories.

items.title: SimFuse3D: Source-Guided Target Simulation and Confidence-Guided Multi-Stage Localization Reweighting for Cross-Platform 3D Object Detection
items.summary: SimFuse3D introduces a new method for cross-platform 3D object detection that uses source-guided target simulation and confidence-guided multi-stage localization reweighting for LiDAR unsupervised domain adaptation. It addresses challenges arising from changes in sensor height and viewpoint.

items.title: InterSing: Explicit Interaction Dynamics for 3D Duet Singing Animation and Beyond
items.summary: InterSing presents a framework for generating realistic 3D head animations for duet singing performances by explicitly modeling interaction dynamics between singers. It enables balancing individual expressiveness with synchronized interaction at musically salient moments.

items.title: Methane Detection On Board Satellites from Unorthorectified Imagery
items.summary: This research presents a method for detecting methane plumes from unorthorectified satellite imagery, which is crucial for climate change mitigation. It offers an alternative to conventional detection methods that rely on orthorectification and matched filters.

items.title: TourPhysics: Bringing Physics to World Models for Exploration and Manipulation from a Single Image
items.summary: TourPhysics introduces a novel approach to integrate physics into visual world models, enabling more robust exploration and manipulation capabilities from a single image. It aims to distinguish between observation and physical intervention, improving understanding of object motion and deformation.

items.title: PuTR-CouT: Counting-by-Tracking in Camera-Trap Image Sequences
items.summary: This paper introduces PuTR-CouT, a counting-by-tracking method designed for camera-trap image sequences to estimate species abundance. It addresses the challenges of low frame rates and lack of counting labels in ecological datasets.

items.title: MultiAttenGastro: Multi-Dimensional Attention Augmentation for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Classification
items.summary: This research proposes MultiAttenGastro, a multi-dimensional attention augmentation framework for automated gastrointestinal endoscopy classification. It aims to improve model generalization across diverse modalities and class distributions in medical imaging.

items.title: VoxelFix: Post-Hoc Semantic Correction of Completed 3D Voxel Maps
items.summary: This paper introduces VoxelFix, a method for post-hoc semantic correction of automatically constructed 3D voxel maps used in aerial robotics. It aims to reduce errors in perception and mapping pipelines to improve map reliability.

items.summary: BurpSqueezer is a tool designed to convert Burp Suite XML dumps into compact, LLM-ready Markdown format, optimizing data for an LLM's context window and efficient information processing.

items.title: CLEAR: Cross-Source Evidence Adjudication for Large Language Models in Medicine
items.summary: CLEAR introduces a method for cross-source evidence adjudication in medical applications of large language models, specifically addressing challenges in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for evolving knowledge.

items.title: Query-Aware Source-Risk Triage for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces Query-Aware Source-Risk Triage, a pre-generation layer for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines that evaluates the material relationship of retrieved sources to the query.

items.title: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
items.summary: EchoPath introduces execution-level replayable memory specifically designed for GUI agents, aiming to improve the efficiency of their observe-plan-ground-act loops.

items.title: LSREP: A Longitudinal State-Replay Protocol for Evaluating Conversational Memory, with ICE v2 as an Audited Local-First Architecture
items.summary: LSREP (Longitudinal State-Replay Evaluation Protocol) is introduced for evaluating conversational memory, focusing on how persistent state accumulates, ages, and incorporates revisions in AI systems.

items.title: ThinkFlow: Self-Evolving Probabilistic Latent Memory for Lifelong Conversational Agents
items.summary: This research presents ThinkFlow, a self-evolving probabilistic latent memory system designed for lifelong conversational agents. It aims to overcome the information bottleneck of explicit textual memory pipelines by capturing subtle behavioral and emotional patterns for more context-aware interactions.

items.title: ORDER: Task-Conditioned Routing for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces ORDER, a task-conditioned routing method for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. It aims to improve RAG performance in domain-expert settings by dynamically adapting indexing and retrieval configurations based on heterogeneous query requirements.

items.title: Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations
items.summary: This research proposes interactive memory learning to enhance long-term conversations for AI agents by developing adaptive memory valuation mechanisms. It aims to move beyond static heuristic paradigms in large language model memory systems.

items.title: Retrieval-Driven Memory Reconsolidation for Long-Term LLM Agents
items.summary: This research introduces a novel memory system for long-term LLM agents that employs retrieval-driven memory reconsolidation. It aims to improve memory evolution by treating retrieval as a driver of updates, rather than just an endpoint of access.

items.title: The Immutable Past: Formalizing State Mutability and Conflict Resolution in Mutable RAG
items.summary: This paper formalizes state mutability and conflict resolution in mutable Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, which serve as primary memory architectures for autonomous agents, to address 'Semantic Shadowing' issues.

items.title: An Organizational Second Brain: Building an AI That Learns from Experts
items.summary: Meta engineers describe the development of an "Organizational Second Brain," an AI system designed to learn from and store knowledge contributed by experts.

items.title: Optimizing cost and latency with Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock introduces prompt caching to optimize cost and latency for foundation models by significantly reducing input token costs for repeated contexts.

items.title: BudgetBench: A Budget-Tiered Protocol and Pilot Harness for Memory Strategy Evaluation in Local Large Language Model Agents
items.summary: BudgetBench is a protocol and harness designed to evaluate memory strategies for local large language model agents, focusing on constraints like active context, memory capacity, and input token limits.

items.title: PolicyMem: Geometric Policy Memory for LLM Governance
items.summary: This paper introduces PolicyMem, a geometric policy memory approach designed to enhance the governance of large language models by providing a new type of safeguard mechanism.

items.title: HyperProve: Answer-Guided Hypergraph Expansion for Multi-Hop Question Answering
items.summary: This paper proposes HyperProve, a retrieval-augmented question answering framework that uses answer-guided hypergraph expansion to improve performance on multi-hop questions by better connecting evidence.

items.title: Towards Evolving Context Parameterization for Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes a method for evolving context parameterization in large language models (LLMs) to allow internalizing contexts into reusable model parameters and distinguishing validity states, addressing limitations of static contexts.

items.title: The Attribution-Compression Frontier in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper explores the trade-offs between context compression and citation attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, measuring how different compression methods impact the traceability of information.

items.title: SpectralShift: Effective Context Window Extension of Gated DeltaNet via Spectral Reparameterization
items.summary: This paper proposes SpectralShift, a method for effectively extending the context window of Gated DeltaNet models for long-context modeling by applying spectral reparameterization to linear attention layers.

items.title: GLAM: Training a latent world model over global spatiotemporal memory for active exploration and navigation
items.summary: This paper presents GLAM, a goal-conditioned latent world model that trains over global spatiotemporal memory to enable active exploration and semantic navigation for embodied AI agents. It focuses on how agents build and use memory from partial observations to plan future actions.

items.title: The generative AI customization spectrum: From prompt engineering to custom models on AWS
items.summary: This article outlines an 8-step decision framework for customizing generative AI on AWS, covering techniques from prompt engineering and fine-tuning to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and continued pre-training.

items.title: The Memory That AI Agents Love
items.summary: This article discusses memory mechanisms preferred by AI agents for storing and recalling information. It explores concepts related to persistent memory in AI systems.

items.title: How DeepSeek V4.1 Achieves a 437x Memory Footprint Drop - Geeky Gadgets
items.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 has achieved a 437x reduction in its memory footprint, detailing improvements in how the AI model stores and utilizes information.

items.title: EAR: Entity-Aware Partitioning Approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Development
items.summary: Presents EAR, an entity-aware partitioning approach designed to improve Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) development by optimizing how source corpora are divided into retrievable units.

items.title: CueMem: Cue-Guided Context Reconstruction for Long-Term Conversational Memory
items.summary: Presents CueMem, a cue-guided context reconstruction method designed to enhance long-term conversational memory for agents by efficiently recalling information from extended dialogue histories.

items.title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents
items.summary: This research introduces LifeMem, a framework to improve large language model agents' ability to reuse past experiences and overcome catastrophic forgetting for lifelong adaptation.

items.title: Cognition on Graph: Navigating Massive Knowledge Space via Cognitive Cycles and Bidirectional Graph-Text Synergy
items.summary: This paper explores 'Cognition on Graph' to enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for LLMs, enabling better navigation and reasoning over massive, heterogeneous knowledge bases.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Retrievers for Polish and European Languages
items.summary: This work proposes a three-stage training pipeline for developing compact and efficient dense retrieval systems, focusing on parameter-efficient models for Polish and other European languages.

items.title: Residual Vector-based Reconstruction as Long-Context Recall Regardless of Context Window Size
items.summary: This research proposes Residual Vector-based Reconstruction as a method for achieving long-context recall in LLMs, aiming to overcome limitations related to context window size.

items.summary: ThreadShelf is presented as a new tool designed to help users search, reuse, and manage their AI chat history from various platforms like OpenRouter, AI Studio, and LM Studio.

items.title: Static state was not enough for a long-running human-AI interaction
items.summary: Research suggests that static state mechanisms are insufficient for managing long-running interactions between humans and AI systems, implying a need for better memory.

items.title: Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces an environment-probing curation method for grounding agent memory in enterprise agents, aiming to prevent the preservation of errors or stale knowledge across sessions.

items.title: MOSAIC: Query-Aware Exploration Policy Adaptation for GraphRAG
items.summary: This paper introduces MOSAIC, a query-aware exploration policy adaptation method for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) systems to improve evidence connection across corpus graphs.

items.title: Memory Compression for High-Fanout Agent Sandboxes
items.summary: This paper addresses the memory bottleneck created by high-fanout agent sandboxes by proposing memory compression techniques that leverage shared templates and related trajectories across concurrent sessions.

items.title: PRAGMA: Evaluating Personalized Guidance with Memory Alignment in Lifelong Conversations
items.summary: This research introduces PRAGMA, a framework for evaluating personalized guidance with memory alignment in lifelong conversations with large language models. It addresses the challenges of inefficient and unreliable long interaction histories in personalized assistants.

items.title: Procedural Memory Under Change: Reuse and Interference in Controlled Web Tasks
items.summary: This study investigates procedural memory in language agents under changing conditions, focusing on the reuse and interference of successful routines in controlled web tasks. It examines how agents adapt when stored routines are no longer applicable.

items.title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization
items.summary: This paper presents kernel-managed shared memory, a system-level abstraction designed for multi-agent AI systems to enable system-wide personalization by allowing specialized agents to share structured, tagged memory.

items.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
items.summary: This research introduces Fortunate Recall, an ontology-driven memory lifecycle management system for LLMs, designed to maintain persistent coherence by strategically managing which memories persist, are replaced, and at what rate.

items.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces ConvMem, a convolutional memory approach to extend the effective context window for Large Language Models by iteratively updating a fixed-size memory based on text segments. This method aims to improve long-context reasoning for LLMs.

items.title: REVA: Reusable Evidence View Aggregation for Context-Efficient RAG Serving
items.summary: This paper introduces REVA (Reusable Evidence View Aggregation), a method designed to improve context efficiency in RAG serving by compressing retrieved documents, thereby reducing latency and memory costs for knowledge-intensive LLM applications.

items.title: FlexComp: One Model for Every Ratio in Context Compression
items.summary: FlexComp introduces a soft context compression technique that condenses context into memory tokens, allowing one model to handle various compression ratios dynamically, unlike existing methods that require separately trained models for each ratio.

items.title: OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs
items.summary: Introduces "OmniKVQuant," a KV cache quantization method specifically for Omni-modal Large Language Models (Omni-LLMs) to reduce their high memory cost, adapting techniques previously used for text-only LLMs.

items.title: 2AM: Grounding Agent-Side Memory as Guidance for Steerable Action Models in Long-Horizon Manipulation

items.summary: This paper introduces MERIT, a new evaluation framework for long-term memory in tool-using LLM agents, focusing on how remembered facts influence agent actions rather than just conversational recall.

items.title: EdgeMem: LLM-Free Agent Memory Construction and Retrieval via Evidence-Preserving Multi-Anchor Hypergraph
items.summary: EdgeMem introduces an LLM-free method for agent memory construction and retrieval using an evidence-preserving multi-anchor hypergraph, aiming to avoid cost and data loss from LLM-generated summaries.

items.title: Recovering Temporal and Geographic Signals from Language Model Embeddings
items.summary: This study investigates how language model embeddings encode temporal and geographic real-world information, using a projection-based method for representation analysis and information retrieval.

items.title: LoGIC: Budgeted Context Construction for Node-Level Graph In-Context Learning with Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper introduces LoGIC, a method for budgeted context construction in node-level graph in-context learning using tabular foundation models. It focuses on how labeled rows serve as prompts and addresses the issue of current protocols employing the complete training table as context.

items.title: Memory in Deep Time-Series Models
items.summary: This work examines the concept of "memory" across various deep learning architectural paradigms for time series models, from recurrent networks and transformers to retrieval-augmented predictors and foundation models. It highlights how these systems store and recall information over time.

items.title: Compressed Recurrent Feedback in Tsetlin Machines: A Reproducible Boolean-FSM Study
items.summary: This study explores compressed recurrent feedback in Tsetlin Machines (RTM) as a mechanism for models to retain useful history for sequential inference on small devices. It describes how RTMs provide memory by feeding Boolean clause outputs from one time step as inputs to the next.

items.title: PACE: Perceived-Latency-Aware Cascading Service Routing and Filler Control for QoE-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Dialogue Serving
items.summary: This paper presents PACE, a framework for retrieval-augmented dialogue serving that optimizes for perceived latency to first response while managing quality and cost constraints.

items.title: Tactile Memory with Soft Robot: Robust Object Insertion via Masked Encoding and Soft Wrist
items.summary: This research introduces TaMeSo-bot, a system that integrates a soft robot wrist with tactile memory and retrieval capabilities to improve robust object insertion in contact-rich tasks.

items.summary: Selmem is an AI memory system developed in Rust that deliberately diverges from Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by intentionally incorporating forgetting and hallucination mechanisms.

items.summary: This research investigates how quantization impacts memory in recurrent neural networks, specifically focusing on recurrent-state write-back in low-precision temporal inference.

items.summary: This paper studies continual graph memory for adaptive recommendation systems that operate under intent drift, using Knowledge Graphs to store and retrieve relational evidence. The memory mechanism helps adapt recommendations based on feedback.

items.summary: This paper proposes "Shadow Queries" to enhance private retrieval in cloud-based vector databases used by large language models (LLMs) for information retrieval systems like RAG.

items.summary: KVMem introduces a system for virtualizing million-token agent workspaces on a consumer GPU, designed to manage the persistent memory and accumulated history of LLM agents. This addresses the challenge of agent context exceeding both GPU KV capacity and the model's native context window.

items.title: BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference
items.summary: This paper introduces BeaconKV, a method for compressing the key-value (KV) cache in large reasoning models. It aims to address memory bottlenecks caused by linearly growing KV caches during extended Chain-of-Thought generation.

items.title: CAGE: Coherence-Aware Graph Encoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces Coherence-Aware Graph Encoding (CAGE), a reranking framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. CAGE models coherence between retrieved chunks to improve the quality of context sets, addressing the issue of individually relevant but collectively incoherent passages.

items.title: NS-ST-GraphRAG: Neuro-Symbolic Spatio-Temporal GraphRAG for Literary Knowledge Processing
items.summary: This paper introduces NS-ST-GraphRAG, a neuro-symbolic spatio-temporal GraphRAG system designed to address the challenges of processing long-form literary narratives for retrieval-augmented generation.

items.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
items.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage training recipe for soft context compression in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to address issues of lengthy retrieved context and improve inference efficiency. items.title: Linguistic Trajectory Encoding for Efficient Long-Horizon Spatial Memory in Embodied Agents
items.summary: This paper proposes Linguistic Trajectory Encoding as a method for efficient long-horizon spatial memory in embodied agents, allowing them to store and recall state transitions of dynamic objects in natural language over extended periods. It addresses the need for fine-grained motion recall beyond typical video-language embeddings.

items.title: EmbodiedLGR: Integrating Lightweight Graph Representation and Retrieval for Semantic-Spatial Memory in Robotic Agents
items.summary: EmbodiedLGR integrates lightweight graph representation and retrieval to provide semantic-spatial memory for robotic agents, enabling efficient information storage and recall in complex environments.

items.title: MHE-Former: Multi-Hypothesis Transformers via Entropy Maximization for 3D Mesh Recovery

items.title: GRADE: Single-Frame Generative Radar Depth Estimation Under Visual Degradation

items.title: Overpainting: Localized Context-aware Diffusion Image Editing

items.title: Harnessing Intrinsic Subject-Aware Attention for Controllable Multi-Subject Video Generation

items.title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization

items.summary: Reducto has released r-1, a new single-pass document parsing model that reduces errors by 20% at a cost of one cent per page.

items.title: WeatherNext 3: Our most advanced global weather AI model
items.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced WeatherNext 3, an advanced global AI model designed for weather prediction.
